verses.ALMEIDA: Se as nuvens estiverem cheias, há chuva sobre a terra; e se a árvore cair, seja para ou sul ou seja para o norte, no lugar em que a árvore cair, ali ela ficará.
verses.RVR09: Si las nubes fueren llenas de agua, sobre la tierra la derramarán: y si el árbol cayere al mediodía, ó al norte, al lugar que el árbol cayere, allí quedará.

verses.KJV: He that observeth the wind shall not sow; and he that regardeth the clouds shall not reap.
verses.WEB: He who observes the wind won’t sow; and he who regards the clouds won’t reap.
verses.ASV: He that observeth the wind shall not sow; and he that regardeth the clouds shall not reap.
verses.ALMEIDA: Quem ficar dando atenção ao vento, nunca semeará; e o que olhar para as nuvens nunca ceifará.
verses.RVR09: El que al viento mira, no sembrará; y el que mira á las nubes, no segará.

verses.KJV: As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit, nor how the bones do grow in the womb of her that is with child: even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.
verses.WEB: As you don’t know what is the way of the wind, nor how the bones grow in the womb of her who is with child; even so you don’t know the work of God who does all.
verses.ASV: As thou knowest not what is the way of the wind, [nor] how the bones [do grow] in the womb of her that is with child; even so thou knowest not the work of God who doeth all.
verses.ALMEIDA: Assim como tu não sabes qual é o caminho do vento, [nem] como se formam os ossos [do feto] no ventre da grávida, assim também tu não sabes a obra de Deus, que faz todas as coisas.
verses.RVR09: Como tú no sabes cuál es el camino del viento, ó cómo se crían los huesos en el vientre de la mujer preñada, así ignoras la obra de Dios, el cual hace todas las cosas.

verses.KJV: In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thine hand: for thou knowest not whether shall prosper, either this or that, or whether they both shall be alike good.
verses.WEB: In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening don’t withhold your hand; for you don’t know which will prosper, whether this or that, or whether they both will be equally good.
verses.ASV: In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thy hand; for thou knowest not which shall prosper, whether this or that, or whether they both shall be alike good.
verses.ALMEIDA: Pela manhã semeia tua semente, e à tarde não retires tua mão; pois tu não sabes qual [tentativa] dará certo, se uma, se outra, ou se ambas [as tentativas] serão boas.
verses.RVR09: Por la mañana siembra tu simiente, y á la tarde no dejes reposar tu mano: porque tú no sabes cuál es lo mejor, si esto ó lo otro, ó si ambas á dos cosas son buenas.

verses.KJV: Truly the light is sweet, and a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to behold the sun:
verses.WEB: Truly the light is sweet, and it is a pleasant thing for the eyes to see the sun.
verses.ASV: Truly the light is sweet, and a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to behold the sun.
verses.ALMEIDA: Certamente a luz é agradável, e ver o sol é bom para os olhos.
verses.RVR09: Suave ciertamente es la luz, y agradable á los ojos ver el sol:

verses.KJV: But if a man live many years, and rejoice in them all; yet let him remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many. All that cometh is vanity.
verses.WEB: Yes, if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all; but let him remember the days of darkness, for they shall be many. All that comes is vanity.
verses.ASV: Yea, if a man live many years, let him rejoice in them all; but let him remember the days of darkness, for they shall be many. All that cometh is vanity.
verses.ALMEIDA: Mesmo se o homem viver muitos anos, [e] em todos eles se alegrar, ele também deve se lembrar dos dias de trevas, porque serão muitos. Tudo o que acontece é futilidade.
verses.RVR09: Mas si el hombre viviere muchos años, y en todos ellos hubiere gozado alegría; si después trajere á la memoria los días de las tinieblas, que serán muchos, todo lo que le habrá pasado, dirá haber sido vanidad.

verses.KJV: Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth; and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thine heart, and in the sight of thine eyes: but know thou, that for all these things God will bring thee into judgment.
verses.WEB: Rejoice, young man, in your youth, and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth, and walk in the ways of your heart, and in the sight of your eyes; but know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.
verses.ASV: Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth, and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thy heart, and in the sight of thine eyes; but know thou, that for all these things God will bring thee into judgment.
verses.ALMEIDA: Alegra-te, rapaz, em tua juventude; e agrada o teu coração nos dias de tua juventude; e anda pelos caminhos do teu coração, e na vista de teus olhos; sabe, porém, que por todas estas coisas, Deus te trará a julgamento.
verses.RVR09: Alégrate, mancebo, en tu mocedad, y tome placer tu corazón en los días de tu juventud; y anda en los caminos de tu corazón, y en la vista de tus ojos: mas sabe, que sobre todas estas cosas te traerá Dios á juicio.

verses.KJV: Therefore remove sorrow from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh: for childhood and youth are vanity.
verses.WEB: Therefore remove sorrow from your heart, and put away evil from your flesh; for youth and the dawn of life are vanity.
verses.ASV: Therefore remove sorrow from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh; for youth and the dawn of life are vanity.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Portanto] afasta o desagrado de teu coração, e tira de tua carne o mal; pois a adolescência e a juventude são futilidade.
verses.RVR09: Quita pues el enojo de tu corazón, y aparta el mal de tu carne: porque la mocedad y la juventud son vanidad.

verses.KJV: Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them;
verses.WEB: Remember also your Creator in the days of your youth, before the evil days come, and the years draw near, when you will say, “I have no pleasure in them;”
verses.ASV: Remember also thy Creator in the days of thy youth, before the evil days come, and the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them;
verses.ALMEIDA: Portanto lembra-te de teu Criador nos dias de tua juventude, antes que venham os dias ruins, e cheguem os anos, dos quais venhas a dizer: Não tenho neles contentamento;
verses.RVR09: Y ACUÉRDATE de tu Criador en los días de tu juventud, antes que vengan los malos días, y lleguen los años, de los cuales digas, No tengo en ellos contentamiento;

verses.KJV: While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain:
verses.WEB: Before the sun, the light, the moon, and the stars are darkened, and the clouds return after the rain;
verses.ASV: before the sun, and the light, and the moon, and the stars, are darkened, and the clouds return after the rain;
verses.ALMEIDA: Antes que se escureçam o sol, a luz, a lua e as estrelas; e voltem as nuvens após a chuva.
verses.RVR09: Antes que se oscurezca el sol, y la luz, y la luna y las estrellas, y las nubes se tornen tras la lluvia:

verses.KJV: In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened,
verses.WEB: in the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those who look out of the windows are darkened,
verses.ASV: in the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows shall be darkened,
verses.ALMEIDA: No dia em que os guardas da casa tremerem, e os homens fortes se encurvarem; e cessarem os moedores, por terem diminuído, e se escurecerem os que olham pelas janelas;
verses.RVR09: Cuando temblarán los guardas de la casa, y se encorvarán los hombres fuertes, y cesarán las muelas, porque han disminuído, y se oscurecerán los que miran por las ventanas;

verses.KJV: And the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musick shall be brought low;
verses.WEB: and the doors shall be shut in the street; when the sound of the grinding is low, and one shall rise up at the voice of a bird, and all the daughters of music shall be brought low;
verses.ASV: and the doors shall be shut in the street; when the sound of the grinding is low, and one shall rise up at the voice of a bird, and all the daughters of music shall be brought low;
verses.ALMEIDA: E as portas da rua se fecharem, enquanto se abaixa o ruído da moedura; e se levantar a voz das aves, e todas as vozes do canto se encurvarem.
verses.RVR09: Y las puertas de afuera se cerrarán, por la bajeza de la voz de la muela; y levantaráse á la voz del ave, y todas las hijas de canción serán humilladas;

verses.KJV: Also when they shall be afraid of that which is high, and fears shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets:
verses.WEB: yes, they shall be afraid of heights, and terrors will be on the way; and the almond tree shall blossom, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail; because man goes to his everlasting home, and the mourners go about the streets;
verses.ASV: yea, they shall be afraid of [that which is] high, and terrors [shall be] in the way; and the almond-tree shall blossom, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail; because man goeth to his everlasting home, and the mourners go about the streets:
verses.ALMEIDA: Como também [quando] temerem as coisas altas, e houver espantos no caminho; e florescer a amendoeira, e o gafanhoto se tornar pesado, e acabar o apetite; porque o homem vai para sua casa eterna, e os que choram andarão ao redor da praça;
verses.RVR09: Cuando también temerán de lo alto, y los tropezones en el camino; y florecerá el almendro, y se agravará la langosta, y perderáse el apetito: porque el hombre va á la casa de su siglo, y los endechadores andarán en derredor por la plaza:

verses.KJV: Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern.
verses.WEB: before the silver cord is severed, or the golden bowl is broken, or the pitcher is broken at the spring, or the wheel broken at the cistern,
verses.ASV: before the silver cord is loosed, or the golden bowl is broken, or the pitcher is broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern,
verses.ALMEIDA: Antes que se afrouxe a correia de prata, e de despedace a vasilha de ouro; e se quebre o vaso junto à fonte, e se despedace a roda junto ao poço.
verses.RVR09: Antes que la cadena de plata se quiebre, y se rompa el cuenco de oro, y el cántaro se quiebre junto á la fuente, y la rueda sea rota sobre el pozo;

verses.KJV: Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.
verses.WEB: and the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
verses.ASV: and the dust returneth to the earth as it was, and the spirit returneth unto God who gave it.
verses.ALMEIDA: E o pó volte à terra, assim como era; e o espírito volte a Deus, que o deu.
verses.RVR09: Y el polvo se torne á la tierra, como era, y el espíritu se vuelva á Dios que lo dió.

verses.KJV: Vanity of vanities, saith the preacher; all is vanity.
verses.WEB: “Vanity of vanities,” says the Preacher. “All is vanity!”
verses.ASV: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher; all is vanity.
verses.ALMEIDA: Futilidade das futilidades! - diz o pregador - Tudo é futilidade.
verses.RVR09: Vanidad de vanidades, dijo el Predicador, todo vanidad.

verses.KJV: And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.
verses.WEB: Further, because the Preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge. Yes, he pondered, sought out, and set in order many proverbs.
verses.ASV: And further, because the Preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he pondered, and sought out, [and] set in order many proverbs.
verses.ALMEIDA: Além do Pregador ter sido sábio, ele também ensinou conhecimento ao povo. Ele ouviu, investigou e pôs em ordem muitos provérbios.
verses.RVR09: Y cuanto más sabio fué el Predicador, tanto más enseñó sabiduría al pueblo; é hizo escuchar, é hizo escudriñar, y compuso muchos proverbios.

verses.KJV: The preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and that which was written was upright, even words of truth.
verses.WEB: The Preacher sought to find out acceptable words, and that which was written blamelessly, words of truth.
verses.ASV: The Preacher sought to find out acceptable words, and that which was written uprightly, [even] words of truth.
verses.ALMEIDA: O Pregador procurou achar palavras agradáveis, e escreveu coisas corretas, palavras de verdade.
verses.RVR09: Procuró el Predicador hallar palabras agradables, y escritura recta, palabras de verdad.

verses.KJV: The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails fastened by the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.
verses.WEB: The words of the wise are like goads; and like nails well fastened are words from the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.
verses.ASV: The words of the wise are as goads; and as nails well fastened are [the words of] the masters of assemblies, [which] are given from one shepherd.
verses.ALMEIDA: As palavras dos sábios são como aguilhões, e como pregos bem fixados [pelos] mestres das congregações, [que] foram dadas pelo único Pastor.
verses.RVR09: Las palabras de los sabios son como aguijones; y como clavos hincados, las de los maestros de las congregaciones, dadas por un Pastor.

verses.KJV: And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.
verses.WEB: Furthermore, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.
verses.ASV: And furthermore, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.
verses.ALMEIDA: Além destas coisas, filho meu, tem cuidado; fazer muitos livros é [algo que] não tem fim; e estudar muito cansa a carne.
verses.RVR09: Ahora, hijo mío, á más de esto, sé avisado. No hay fin de hacer muchos libros; y el mucho estudio aflicción es de la carne.

verses.KJV: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.
verses.WEB: This is the end of the matter. All has been heard. Fear God and keep his commandments; for this is the whole duty of man.
verses.ASV: [This is] the end of the matter; all hath been heard: Fear God, and keep his commandments; for this is the whole [duty] of man.
verses.ALMEIDA: De tudo o que foi ouvido, a conclusão é: teme a Deus, e guarda os mandamentos dele; porque isto é [o dever de] todo homem.
verses.RVR09: El fin de todo el discurso oído es este: Teme á Dios, y guarda sus mandamientos; porque esto es el todo del hombre.

verses.KJV: For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.
verses.WEB: For God will bring every work into judgment, with every hidden thing, whether it is good, or whether it is evil.
verses.ASV: For God will bring every work into judgment, with every hidden thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.
verses.ALMEIDA: Porque Deus trará a julgamento toda obra, até mesmo tudo o que está encoberto, seja bom ou mal.
verses.RVR09: Porque Dios traerá toda obra á juicio, el cual se hará sobre toda cosa oculta, buena ó mala.

verses.KJV: The song of songs, which is Solomon's.
verses.WEB: The Song of songs, which is Solomon’s.
verses.ASV: The Song of songs, which is Solomon’s.
verses.ALMEIDA: Cântico dos cânticos, que é de Salomão.
verses.RVR09: CANCIÓN de canciones, la cual es de Salomón.

verses.KJV: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: for thy love is better than wine.
verses.WEB: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth; for your love is better than wine.
verses.ASV: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth; For thy love is better than wine.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Ela] : Beije-me ele com os beijos de sua boca, porque teu amor é melhor do que o vinho.
verses.RVR09: ¡Oh si él me besara con ósculos de su boca! porque mejores son tus amores que el vino.

verses.KJV: Because of the savour of thy good ointments thy name is as ointment poured forth, therefore do the virgins love thee.
verses.WEB: Your oils have a pleasing fragrance. Your name is oil poured out, therefore the virgins love you.
verses.ASV: Thine oils have a goodly fragrance; Thy name is [as] oil poured forth; Therefore do the virgins love thee.
verses.ALMEIDA: O cheiro dos teus perfumes é agradável; teu nome é [como] perfume sendo derramado, por isso as virgens te amam.
verses.RVR09: Por el olor de tus suaves ungüentos, (ungüento derramado es tu nombre,) por eso las doncellas te amaron.

verses.KJV: Draw me, we will run after thee: the king hath brought me into his chambers: we will be glad and rejoice in thee, we will remember thy love more than wine: the upright love thee.
verses.WEB: Take me away with you. Let’s hurry. The king has brought me into his rooms. Friends We will be glad and rejoice in you. We will praise your love more than wine! Beloved They are right to love you.
verses.ASV: Draw me; we will run after thee: The king hath brought me into his chambers; We will be glad and rejoice in thee; We will make mention of thy love more than of wine: Rightly do they love thee.
verses.ALMEIDA: Toma-me contigo, e corramos; traga-me o rei aos seus quartos.[Moças] : Em ti nos alegraremos e nos encheremos de alegria; nos agradaremos mais de teu amor do que do vinho;[Ela] : Elas estão certas em te amar;
verses.RVR09: Llévame en pos de ti, correremos. Metióme el rey en sus cámaras: nos gozaremos y alegraremos en ti; acordarémonos de tus amores más que del vino: los rectos te aman.

verses.KJV: I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon.
verses.WEB: I am dark, but lovely, you daughters of Jerusalem, like Kedar’s tents, like Solomon’s curtains.
verses.ASV: I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, As the tents of Kedar, As the curtains of Solomon.
verses.ALMEIDA: Eu sou morena, porém bela, ó filhas de Jerusalém: [morena] como as tendas de Quedar, [bela] como as cortinas de Salomão.
verses.RVR09: Morena soy, oh hijas de Jerusalem, mas codiciable; como las cabañas de Cedar, como las tiendas de Salomón.

verses.KJV: Look not upon me, because I am black, because the sun hath looked upon me: my mother's children were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vineyards; but mine own vineyard have I not kept.
verses.WEB: Don’t stare at me because I am dark, because the sun has scorched me. My mother’s sons were angry with me. They made me keeper of the vineyards. I haven’t kept my own vineyard.
verses.ASV: Look not upon me, because I am swarthy, Because the sun hath scorched me. My mother’s sons were incensed against me; They made me keeper of the vineyards; [But] mine own vineyard have I not kept.
verses.ALMEIDA: Não fiquem me olhando por eu ser morena, pois o sol brilhou sobre mim; os filhos de minha mãe se irritaram contra mim, [e] me puseram para cuidar de vinhas; [porém] minha própria vinha, que me pertence, não cuidei.
verses.RVR09: No miréis en que soy morena, porque el sol me miró. Los hijos de mi madre se airaron contra mí, hiciéronme guarda de viñas; y mi viña, que era mía, no guardé.

verses.KJV: Tell me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou makest thy flock to rest at noon: for why should I be as one that turneth aside by the flocks of thy companions?
verses.WEB: Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where you graze your flock, where you rest them at noon; for why should I be as one who is veiled beside the flocks of your companions?
verses.ASV: Tell me, O thou whom my soul loveth, Where thou feedest [thy flock], Where thou makest [it] to rest at noon: For why should I be as one that is veiled Beside the flocks of thy companions?
verses.ALMEIDA: Dize-me, amado de minha alma: onde apascentas [o teu gado] ? Onde [o] recolhes ao meio- dia? Para que ficaria eu como que coberta com um véu por entre os gados de teus colegas?
verses.RVR09: Hazme saber, ó tú á quien ama mi alma, dónde repastas, dónde haces tener majada al medio día: porque, ¿por qué había yo de estar como vagueando tras los rebaños de tus compañeros?

verses.KJV: If thou know not, O thou fairest among women, go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, and feed thy kids beside the shepherds' tents.
verses.WEB: If you don’t know, most beautiful among women, follow the tracks of the sheep. Graze your young goats beside the shepherds’ tents.
verses.ASV: If thou know not, O thou fairest among women, Go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, And feed thy kids beside the shepherds’ tents.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Ele] : Se tu, a mais bela entre as mulheres, não sabes, sai pelos rastros das ovelhas, e apascenta tuas cabras junto às tendas dos pastores.
verses.RVR09: Si tú no lo sabes, oh hermosa entre las mujeres, sal, yéndote por las huellas del rebaño, y apacienta tus cabritas junto á las cabañas de los pastores.

verses.KJV: I have compared thee, O my love, to a company of horses in Pharaoh's chariots.
verses.WEB: I have compared you, my love, to a steed in Pharaoh’s chariots.
verses.ASV: I have compared thee, O my love, To a steed in Pharaoh’s chariots.
verses.ALMEIDA: Eu te comparo, querida, às éguas das carruagens de Faraó.
verses.RVR09: A yegua de los carros de Faraón te he comparado, amiga mía.

verses.KJV: Thy cheeks are comely with rows of jewels, thy neck with chains of gold.
verses.WEB: Your cheeks are beautiful with earrings, your neck with strings of jewels.
verses.ASV: Thy cheeks are comely with plaits [of hair], Thy neck with strings of jewels.
verses.ALMEIDA: Agradáveis são tuas laterais da face entre os enfeites, teu pescoço entre os colares.
verses.RVR09: Hermosas son tus mejillas entre los pendientes, tu cuello entre los collares.

verses.KJV: We will make thee borders of gold with studs of silver.
verses.WEB: We will make you earrings of gold, with studs of silver.
verses.ASV: We will make thee plaits of gold With studs of silver.
verses.ALMEIDA: Enfeites de ouro faremos para ti, com detalhes de prata.
verses.RVR09: Zarcillos de oro te haremos, con clavos de plata.

verses.KJV: While the king sitteth at his table, my spikenard sendeth forth the smell thereof.
verses.WEB: While the king sat at his table, my perfume spread its fragrance.
verses.ASV: While the king sat at his table, My spikenard sent forth its fragrance.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Ela] : Enquanto o rei está sentado à sua mesa, meu nardo dá a sua fragrância.
verses.RVR09: Mientras que el rey estaba en su reclinatorio, mi nardo dió su olor.

verses.KJV: A bundle of myrrh is my well-beloved unto me; he shall lie all night betwixt my breasts.
verses.WEB: My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh, that lies between my breasts.
verses.ASV: My beloved is unto me [as] a bundle of myrrh, That lieth betwixt my breasts.
verses.ALMEIDA: Meu amado é para mim [como] um saquinho de mirra que passa a noite entre meus seios;
verses.RVR09: Mi amado es para mí un manojito de mirra, que reposa entre mis pechos.

verses.KJV: My beloved is unto me as a cluster of camphire in the vineyards of Engedi.
verses.WEB: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms from the vineyards of En Gedi.
verses.ASV: My beloved is unto me [as] a cluster of henna-flowers In the vineyards of En-gedi.
verses.ALMEIDA: Meu amado é para mim [como] um ramalhete de hena nas vinhas de Engedi.
verses.RVR09: Racimo de copher en las viñas de Engadi es para mí mi amado.

verses.KJV: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves' eyes.
verses.WEB: Behold, you are beautiful, my love. Behold, you are beautiful. Your eyes are like doves.
verses.ASV: Behold, thou art fair, my love; Behold thou art fair; Thine eyes are [as] doves.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Ele] : Como tu és bela, minha querida! Como tu és bela! Teus olhos são [como] pombas.
verses.RVR09: He aquí que tú eres hermosa, amiga mía; he aquí que eres bella: tus ojos de paloma.

verses.KJV: Behold, thou art fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant: also our bed is green.
verses.WEB: Behold, you are beautiful, my beloved, yes, pleasant; and our couch is verdant.
verses.ASV: Behold, thou art fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant: Also our couch is green.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Ela] : Como tu és belo, meu amado! Como [tu és] agradável! E o nosso leito se enche de folhagens.
verses.RVR09: He aquí que tú eres hermoso, amado mío, y suave: nuestro lecho también florido.

verses.KJV: The beams of our house are cedar, and our rafters of fir.
verses.WEB: The beams of our house are cedars. Our rafters are firs.
verses.ASV: The beams of our house are cedars, [And] our rafters are firs.
verses.ALMEIDA: As vigas de nossa casa são os cedros, e nossos caibros os ciprestes.
verses.RVR09: Las vigas de nuestra casa son de cedro, y de ciprés los artesonados.

verses.KJV: I am the rose of Sharon, and the lily of the valleys.
verses.WEB: I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.
verses.ASV: I am a rose of Sharon, A lily of the valleys.
verses.ALMEIDA: Eu sou a rosa de Sarom, o lírio dos vales.
verses.RVR09: YO soy la rosa de Sarón, y el lirio de los valles.

verses.KJV: As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.
verses.WEB: As a lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.
verses.ASV: As a lily among thorns, So is my love among the daughters.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Ele] : Como um lírio entre os espinhos, assim é minha querida entre as moças.
verses.RVR09: Como el lirio entre las espinas, así es mi amiga entre las doncellas.

verses.KJV: As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.
verses.WEB: As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, his fruit was sweet to my taste.
verses.ASV: As the apple-tree among the trees of the wood, So is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, And his fruit was sweet to my taste.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Ela] : Como a macieira entre as árvores do bosque, assim é o meu amado entre os rapazes; debaixo de sua sombra desejo muito sentar, e doce é o seu fruto ao meu paladar.
verses.RVR09: Como el manzano entre los árboles silvestres, así es mi amado entre los mancebos: bajo la sombra del deseado me senté, y su fruto fué dulce á mi paladar.

verses.KJV: He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me was love.
verses.WEB: He brought me to the banquet hall. His banner over me is love.
verses.ASV: He brought me to the banqueting-house, And his banner over me was love.
verses.ALMEIDA: Ele me leva à casa do banquete, e sua bandeira sobre mim é o amor.
verses.RVR09: Llevóme á la cámara del vino, y su bandera sobre mí fué amor.

verses.KJV: Stay me with flagons, comfort me with apples: for I am sick of love.
verses.WEB: Strengthen me with raisins, refresh me with apples; for I am faint with love.
verses.ASV: Stay ye me with raisins, refresh me with apples; For I am sick from love.
verses.ALMEIDA: Sustentai-me com passas, fortalecei-me com maçãs; porque estou fraca de amor.
verses.RVR09: Sustentadme con frascos, corroboradme con manzanas; porque estoy enferma de amor.

verses.KJV: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand doth embrace me.
verses.WEB: His left hand is under my head. His right hand embraces me.
verses.ASV: His left hand [is] under my head, And his right hand doth embrace me.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Esteja] sua mão esquerda abaixo de minha cabeça, e sua direita me abraça.
verses.RVR09: Su izquierda esté debajo de mi cabeza, y su derecha me abrace.

verses.KJV: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.
verses.WEB: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, or by the hinds of the field, that you not stir up, nor awaken love, until it so desires.
verses.ASV: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, By the roes, or by the hinds of the field, That ye stir not up, nor awake [my] love, Until he please.
verses.ALMEIDA: Eu vos ordeno, filhas de Jerusalém: jurai pelas corças e pelas cervas do campo, que não acordeis, nem desperteis ao amor, até que ele queira.
verses.RVR09: Yo os conjuro, oh doncellas de Jerusalem, por las gamas y por las ciervas del campo, que no despertéis ni hagáis velar al amor, hasta que quiera.

verses.KJV: The voice of my beloved! behold, he cometh leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills.
verses.WEB: The voice of my beloved! Behold, he comes, leaping on the mountains, skipping on the hills.
verses.ASV: The voice of my beloved! behold, he cometh, Leaping upon the mountains, Skipping upon the hills.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Esta é] a voz do meu amado: vede-o vindo, saltando sobre os montes, pulando sobre os morros.
verses.RVR09: ¡La voz de mi amado! He aquí él viene saltando sobre los montes, brincando sobre los collados.

verses.KJV: My beloved is like a roe or a young hart: behold, he standeth behind our wall, he looketh forth at the windows, shewing himself through the lattice.
verses.WEB: My beloved is like a roe or a young deer. Behold, he stands behind our wall! He looks in at the windows. He glances through the lattice.
verses.ASV: My beloved is like a roe or a young hart: Behold, he standeth behind our wall; He looketh in at the windows; He glanceth through the lattice.
verses.ALMEIDA: Meu amado é semelhante ao corço, ou ao filhote de cervos; eis que está atrás de nossa parede, olhando pelas janelas, observando pelas grades.
verses.RVR09: Mi amado es semejante al gamo, ó al cabrito de los ciervos. Helo aquí, está tras nuestra pared, mirando por las ventanas, mostrándose por las rejas.

verses.KJV: My beloved spake, and said unto me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.
verses.WEB: My beloved spoke, and said to me, “Rise up, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.
verses.ASV: My beloved spake, and said unto me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.
verses.ALMEIDA: Meu amado me responde, e me diz:[Ele] : Levanta-te, querida minha, minha bela, e vem.
verses.RVR09: Mi amado habló, y me dijo: Levántate, oh amiga mía, hermosa mía, y vente.

verses.KJV: For, lo, the winter is past, the rain is over and gone;
verses.WEB: For behold, the winter is past. The rain is over and gone.
verses.ASV: For, lo, the winter is past; The rain is over and gone;
verses.ALMEIDA: Porque eis que o inverno já passou; a chuva se acabou, e foi embora.
verses.RVR09: Porque he aquí ha pasado el invierno, hase mudado, la lluvia se fué;

verses.KJV: The flowers appear on the earth; the time of the singing of birds is come, and the voice of the turtle is heard in our land;
verses.WEB: The flowers appear on the earth. The time of the singing has come, and the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.
verses.ASV: The flowers appear on the earth; The time of the singing [of birds] is come, And the voice of the turtle-dove is heard in our land;
verses.ALMEIDA: As flores aparecem na terra, o tempo da cantoria chegou; e ouve-se a voz da rolinha em nossa terra.
verses.RVR09: Hanse mostrado las flores en la tierra, el tiempo de la canción es venido, y en nuestro país se ha oído la voz de la tórtola;

verses.KJV: The fig tree putteth forth her green figs, and the vines with the tender grape give a good smell. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away.
verses.WEB: The fig tree ripens her green figs. The vines are in blossom. They give out their fragrance. Arise, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.”
verses.ASV: The fig-tree ripeneth her green figs, And the vines are in blossom; They give forth their fragrance. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away.
verses.ALMEIDA: A figueira está produzindo seus figos verdes, e as vides florescentes dão cheiro; levanta-te, querida minha, minha bela, e vem.
verses.RVR09: La higuera ha echado sus higos, y las vides en cierne dieron olor: levántate, oh amiga mía, hermosa mía, y vente.

verses.KJV: O my dove, that art in the clefts of the rock, in the secret places of the stairs, let me see thy countenance, let me hear thy voice; for sweet is thy voice, and thy countenance is comely.
verses.WEB: My dove in the clefts of the rock, in the hiding places of the mountainside, let me see your face. Let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet and your face is lovely.
verses.ASV: O my dove, that art in the clefts of the rock, In the covert of the steep place, Let me see thy countenance, Let me hear thy voice; For sweet is thy voice, and thy countenance is comely.
verses.ALMEIDA: Pomba minha, que andas pelas fendas das rochas no oculto das ladeiras, mostra-me tua face, faze-me ouvir tua voz; porque tua voz é doce, e tua face agradável.
verses.RVR09: Paloma mía, que estás en los agujeros de la peña, en lo escondido de escarpados parajes, muéstrame tu rostro, hazme oir tu voz; porque dulce es la voz tuya, y hermoso tu aspecto.

verses.KJV: Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines have tender grapes.
verses.WEB: Catch for us the foxes, the little foxes that plunder the vineyards; for our vineyards are in blossom.
verses.ASV: Take us the foxes, the little foxes, That spoil the vineyards; For our vineyards are in blossom.
verses.ALMEIDA: Tomai-nos as raposas, as raposinhas, que danificam as vinhas, porque nossas vinhas estão florescendo.
verses.RVR09: Cazadnos las zorras, las zorras pequeñas, que echan á perder las viñas; pues que nuestras viñas están en cierne.

verses.KJV: My beloved is mine, and I am his: he feedeth among the lilies.
verses.WEB: My beloved is mine, and I am his. He browses among the lilies.
verses.ASV: My beloved is mine, and I am his: He feedeth [his flock] among the lilies.
verses.ALMEIDA: Meu amado é meu, e eu sou sua; ele apascenta entre os lírios.
verses.RVR09: Mi amado es mío, y yo suya; él apacienta entre lirios.

verses.KJV: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be thou like a roe or a young hart upon the mountains of Bether.
verses.WEB: Until the day is cool, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be like a roe or a young deer on the mountains of Bether.
verses.ASV: Until the day be cool, and the shadows flee away, Turn, my beloved, and be thou like a roe or a young hart Upon the mountains of Bether.
verses.ALMEIDA: Antes do dia se romper, e das sombras fugirem, volta, amado meu, faze-te semelhante ao corço, ao filhote de cervos, sobre os montes de Beter.
verses.RVR09: Hasta que apunte el día, y huyan las sombras, tórnate, amado mío; sé semejante al gamo, ó al cabrito de los ciervos, sobre los montes de Bether.

verses.KJV: By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
verses.WEB: By night on my bed, I sought him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him.
verses.ASV: By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Ela] :Durante as noites busquei em minha cama a quem minha alma ama; busquei-o, mas não o achei.
verses.RVR09: POR las noches busqué en mi lecho al que ama mi alma: busquélo, y no lo hallé.

verses.KJV: I will rise now, and go about the city in the streets, and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
verses.WEB: I will get up now, and go about the city; in the streets and in the squares I will seek him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him.
verses.ASV: [I said], I will rise now, and go about the city; In the streets and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
verses.ALMEIDA: Por isso me levantarei, e percorrerei a cidade, pelas ruas e pelas praças; buscarei a quem minha alma ama; busquei-o, mas não o achei.
verses.RVR09: Levantaréme ahora, y rodearé por la ciudad; por las calles y por las plazas buscaré al que ama mi alma: busquélo, y no lo hallé.

verses.KJV: The watchmen that go about the city found me: to whom I said, Saw ye him whom my soul loveth?
verses.WEB: The watchmen who go about the city found me; “Have you seen him whom my soul loves?”
verses.ASV: The watchmen that go about the city found me; [To whom I said], Saw ye him whom my soul loveth?
verses.ALMEIDA: Os guardas que rondavam pela cidade me encontraram. [Eu lhes perguntei] : Vistes a quem minha alma ama?
verses.RVR09: Halláronme los guardas que rondan la ciudad, y díjeles: ¿Habéis visto al que ama mi alma?

verses.KJV: It was but a little that I passed from them, but I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother's house, and into the chamber of her that conceived me.
verses.WEB: I had scarcely passed from them, when I found him whom my soul loves. I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother’s house, into the room of her who conceived me.
verses.ASV: It was but a little that I passed from them, When I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him go, Until I had brought him into my mother’s house, And into the chamber of her that conceived me.
verses.ALMEIDA: Pouco [depois] de me afastar deles, logo achei a quem minha alma ama. Eu o segurei, e não o deixei ir embora, até eu ter lhe trazido à casa de minha mãe, ao cômodo daquela que me gerou.
verses.RVR09: Pasando de ellos un poco, hallé luego al que mi alma ama: trabé de él, y no lo dejé, hasta que lo metí en casa de mi madre, y en la cámara de la que me engendró.

verses.KJV: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.
verses.WEB: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, or by the hinds of the field, that you not stir up nor awaken love, until it so desires.
verses.ASV: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, By the roes, or by the hinds of the field, That ye stir not up, nor awake [my] love, Until he please.
verses.ALMEIDA: Eu vos ordeno, filhas de Jerusalém: jurai pelas corças e pelas cervas do campo que não acordeis nem desperteis ao amor, até que ele queira.
verses.RVR09: Yo os conjuro, oh doncellas de Jerusalem, por las gamas y por las ciervas del campo, que no despertéis ni hagáis velar al amor, hasta que quiera.

verses.KJV: Who is this that cometh out of the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all powders of the merchant?
verses.WEB: Who is this who comes up from the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all spices of the merchant?
verses.ASV: Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness Like pillars of smoke, Perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, With all powders of the merchant?
verses.ALMEIDA: Quem é esta, que sobe do deserto como colunas de fumaça, perfumada com mirra, incenso, e com todo tipo de pó aromático de mercador?
verses.RVR09: ¿Quién es ésta que sube del desierto como columnita de humo, sahumada de mirra y de incienso, y de todos polvos aromáticos?

verses.KJV: Behold his bed, which is Solomon's; threescore valiant men are about it, of the valiant of Israel.
verses.WEB: Behold, it is Solomon’s carriage! Sixty mighty men are around it, of the mighty men of Israel.
verses.ASV: Behold, it is the litter of Solomon; Threescore mighty men are about it, Of the mighty men of Israel.
verses.ALMEIDA: Eis a cama móvel de Salomão! Sessenta guerreiros estão ao redor dela, dentre os guerreiros de Israel;
verses.RVR09: He aquí es la litera de Salomón: sesenta valientes la rodean, de los fuertes de Israel.

verses.KJV: They all hold swords, being expert in war: every man hath his sword upon his thigh because of fear in the night.
verses.WEB: They all handle the sword, and are expert in war. Every man has his sword on his thigh, because of fear in the night.
verses.ASV: They all handle the sword, [and] are expert in war: Every man hath his sword upon his thigh, Because of fear in the night.
verses.ALMEIDA: Todos eles portando espadas, habilidosos na guerra; cada um com sua espada à cintura, para [o caso de haver] um ataque repentino de noite.
verses.RVR09: Todos ellos tienen espadas, diestros en la guerra; cada uno su espada sobre su muslo, por los temores de la noche.

verses.KJV: King Solomon made himself a chariot of the wood of Lebanon.
verses.WEB: King Solomon made himself a carriage of the wood of Lebanon.
verses.ASV: King Solomon made himself a palanquin Of the wood of Lebanon.
verses.ALMEIDA: O rei Salomão fez para si uma liteira de madeira do Líbano.
verses.RVR09: El rey Salomón se hizo una carroza de madera del Líbano.

verses.KJV: He made the pillars thereof of silver, the bottom thereof of gold, the covering of it of purple, the midst thereof being paved with love, for the daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.WEB: He made its pillars of silver, its bottom of gold, its seat of purple, the middle of it being paved with love, from the daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.ASV: He made the pillars thereof of silver, The bottom thereof of gold, the seat of it of purple, The midst thereof being paved with love, From the daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.ALMEIDA: Suas colunas ele fez de prata, seu assoalho de ouro, seu assento de púrpura; por dentro coberta com [a obra do] amor das filhas de Jerusalém.
verses.RVR09: Sus columnas hizo de plata, su respaldo de oro, su cielo de grana, su interior enlosado de amor, por las doncellas de Jerusalem.

verses.KJV: Go forth, O ye daughters of Zion, and behold king Solomon with the crown wherewith his mother crowned him in the day of his espousals, and in the day of the gladness of his heart.
verses.WEB: Go out, you daughters of Zion, and see King Solomon, with the crown with which his mother has crowned him, in the day of his weddings, in the day of the gladness of his heart.
verses.ASV: Go forth, O ye daughters of Zion, and behold king Solomon, With the crown wherewith his mother hath crowned him In the day of his espousals, And in the day of the gladness of his heart.
verses.ALMEIDA: Saí, ó filhas de Sião, e contemplai ao rei Salomão, com a coroa a qual sua mãe o coroou, no dia de seu casamento, no dia da alegria do seu coração.
verses.RVR09: Salid, oh doncellas de Sión, y ved al rey Salomón con la corona con que le coronó su madre el día de su desposorio, y el día del gozo de su corazón.

verses.KJV: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves' eyes within thy locks: thy hair is as a flock of goats, that appear from mount Gilead.
verses.WEB: Behold, you are beautiful, my love. Behold, you are beautiful. Your eyes are like doves behind your veil. Your hair is as a flock of goats, that descend from Mount Gilead.
verses.ASV: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; Thine eyes are [as] doves behind thy veil. Thy hair is as a flock of goats, That lie along the side of mount Gilead.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Ele] : Como tu és bela, minha querida! Como tu és bela! Teus olhos por trás do véu são [como] pombas; teu cabelo é como um rebanho de cabras, que descem do monte Gileade.
verses.RVR09: HE aquí que tú eres hermosa, amiga mía; he aquí que tú eres hermosa; tus ojos entre tus guedejas como de paloma; tus cabellos como manada de cabras, que se muestran desde el monte de Galaad.

verses.KJV: Thy teeth are like a flock of sheep that are even shorn, which came up from the washing; whereof every one bear twins, and none is barren among them.
verses.WEB: Your teeth are like a newly shorn flock, which have come up from the washing, where every one of them has twins. None is bereaved among them.
verses.ASV: Thy teeth are like a flock [of ewes] that are [newly] shorn, Which are come up from the washing, Whereof every one hath twins, And none is bereaved among them.
verses.ALMEIDA: Teus dentes são como [ovelhas] tosquiadas, que sobem do lavatório; todas elas têm gêmeos, e nenhuma delas é estéril.
verses.RVR09: Tus dientes, como manadas de trasquiladas ovejas, que suben del lavadero, todas con crías mellizas, y ninguna entre ellas estéril.

verses.KJV: Thy lips are like a thread of scarlet, and thy speech is comely: thy temples are like a piece of a pomegranate within thy locks.
verses.WEB: Your lips are like scarlet thread. Your mouth is lovely. Your temples are like a piece of a pomegranate behind your veil.
verses.ASV: Thy lips are like a thread of scarlet, And thy mouth is comely. Thy temples are like a piece of a pomegranate Behind thy veil.
verses.ALMEIDA: Teus lábios são como uma fita de escarlate, e tua boca é bonita; tuas têmporas são como pedaços de romã por detrás do véu.
verses.RVR09: Tus labios, como un hilo de grana, y tu habla hermosa; tus sienes, como cachos de granada á la parte adentro de tus guedejas.

verses.KJV: Thy neck is like the tower of David builded for an armoury, whereon there hang a thousand bucklers, all shields of mighty men.
verses.WEB: Your neck is like David’s tower built for an armory, on which a thousand shields hang, all the shields of the mighty men.
verses.ASV: Thy neck is like the tower of David Builded for an armory, Whereon there hang a thousand bucklers, All the shields of the mighty men.
verses.ALMEIDA: Teu pescoço é como a torre de Davi, construída como fortaleza; mil escudos estão nela pendurados, todos escudos de guerreiros.
verses.RVR09: Tu cuello, como la torre de David, edificada para muestra; mil escudos están colgados de ella, todos escudos de valientes.

verses.KJV: Thy two breasts are like two young roes that are twins, which feed among the lilies.
verses.WEB: Your two breasts are like two fawns that are twins of a roe, which feed among the lilies.
verses.ASV: Thy two breasts are like two fawns That are twins of a roe, Which feed among the lilies.
verses.ALMEIDA: Teus dois seios são como dois filhos gêmeos da corça, que pastam entre os lírios.
verses.RVR09: Tus dos pechos, como dos cabritos mellizos de gama, que son apacentados entre azucenas.

verses.KJV: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.
verses.WEB: Until the day is cool, and the shadows flee away, I will go to the mountain of myrrh, to the hill of frankincense.
verses.ASV: Until the day be cool, and the shadows flee away, I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, And to the hill of frankincense.
verses.ALMEIDA: Antes do dia nascer, e das sombras fugirem, irei ao monte de mirra, e ao morro do incenso.
verses.RVR09: Hasta que apunte el día y huyan las sombras, iréme al monte de la mirra, y al collado del incienso.

verses.KJV: Thou art all fair, my love; there is no spot in thee.
verses.WEB: You are all beautiful, my love. There is no spot in you.
verses.ASV: Thou art all fair, my love; And there is no spot in thee.
verses.ALMEIDA: Tu és bela, minha querida! Não há defeito algum em ti.
verses.RVR09: Toda tú eres hermosa, amiga mía, y en ti no hay mancha.

verses.KJV: Come with me from Lebanon, my spouse, with me from Lebanon: look from the top of Amana, from the top of Shenir and Hermon, from the lions' dens, from the mountains of the leopards.
verses.WEB: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, with me from Lebanon. Look from the top of Amana, from the top of Senir and Hermon, from the lions’ dens, from the mountains of the leopards.
verses.ASV: Come with me from Lebanon, [my] bride, With me from Lebanon: Look from the top of Amana, From the top of Senir and Hermon, From the lions’ dens, From the mountains of the leopards.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Vem] comigo do Líbano, ó esposa minha, vem comigo do Líbano; desce do cume de Amaná, do cume de Senir e de Hermom, das montanhas das leoas, dos montes dos leopardos.
verses.RVR09: Conmigo del Líbano, oh esposa, conmigo ven del Líbano: mira desde la cumbre de Amana, desde la cumbre de Senir y de Hermón, desde las guaridas de los leones, desde los montes de los tigres.

verses.KJV: Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister, my spouse; thou hast ravished my heart with one of thine eyes, with one chain of thy neck.
verses.WEB: You have ravished my heart, my sister, my bride. You have ravished my heart with one of your eyes, with one chain of your neck.
verses.ASV: Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister, [my] bride; Thou hast ravished my heart with one of thine eyes, With one chain of thy neck.
verses.ALMEIDA: Tomaste meu coração, minha irmã, minha esposa; tomaste o meu coração com um de teus olhos, com um colar de teu pescoço.
verses.RVR09: Prendiste mi corazón, hermana, esposa mía; has preso mi corazón con uno de tus ojos, con una gargantilla de tu cuello.

verses.KJV: How fair is thy love, my sister, my spouse! how much better is thy love than wine! and the smell of thine ointments than all spices!
verses.WEB: How beautiful is your love, my sister, my bride! How much better is your love than wine, the fragrance of your perfumes than all kinds of spices!
verses.ASV: How fair is thy love, my sister, [my] bride! How much better is thy love than wine! And the fragrance of thine oils than all manner of spices!
verses.ALMEIDA: Como são agradáveis os teus amores, minha irmã, minha esposa! São bem melhores do que o vinho; e o cheiro de teus unguentos [é melhor] que todas as especiarias.
verses.RVR09: ¡Cuán hermosos son tus amores, hermana, esposa mía! ¡cuánto mejores que el vino tus amores, y el olor de tus ungüentos que todas las especias aromáticas!

verses.KJV: Thy lips, O my spouse, drop as the honeycomb: honey and milk are under thy tongue; and the smell of thy garments is like the smell of Lebanon.
verses.WEB: Your lips, my bride, drip like the honeycomb. Honey and milk are under your tongue. The smell of your garments is like the smell of Lebanon.
verses.ASV: Thy lips, O [my] bride, drop [as] the honeycomb: Honey and milk are under thy tongue; And the smell of thy garments is like the smell of Lebanon.
verses.ALMEIDA: Favos de mel descem de teus lábios, ó esposa; mel e leite estão debaixo de tua língua; e o cheiro de teus vestidos é como o cheiro do Líbano.
verses.RVR09: Como panal de miel destilan tus labios, oh esposa; miel y leche hay debajo de tu lengua; y el olor de tus vestidos como el olor del Líbano.

verses.KJV: A garden inclosed is my sister, my spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.
verses.WEB: My sister, my bride, is a locked up garden; a locked up spring, a sealed fountain.
verses.ASV: A garden shut up is my sister, [my] bride; A spring shut up, a fountain sealed.
verses.ALMEIDA: Jardim fechado és tu, minha irmã, minha esposa; manancial fechado, uma fonte selada.
verses.RVR09: Huerto cerrado eres, mi hermana, esposa mía; fuente cerrada, fuente sellada.

verses.KJV: Thy plants are an orchard of pomegranates, with pleasant fruits; camphire, with spikenard,
verses.WEB: Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates, with precious fruits, henna with spikenard plants,
verses.ASV: Thy shoots are an orchard of pomegranates, with precious fruits; Henna with spikenard plants,
verses.ALMEIDA: Tuas plantas são uma horta de romãs, com frutos excelentes: hena e nardo.
verses.RVR09: Tus renuevos paraíso de granados, con frutos suaves, de cámphoras y nardos,

verses.KJV: Spikenard and saffron; calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices:
verses.WEB: spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of incense tree; myrrh and aloes, with all the best spices,
verses.ASV: Spikenard and saffron, Calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; Myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices.
verses.ALMEIDA: Nardo, açafrão, cálamo e canela; com todo tipo de árvores de incenso: mirra, aloés, com todas as melhores especiarias.
verses.RVR09: Nardo y azafrán, caña aromática y canela, con todos los árboles de incienso; mirra y áloes, con todas las principales especias.

verses.KJV: A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon.
verses.WEB: a fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, flowing streams from Lebanon.
verses.ASV: [Thou art] a fountain of gardens, A well of living waters, And flowing streams from Lebanon.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Tu és] uma fonte de jardins, um poço de águas vivas que corre do Líbano.
verses.RVR09: Fuente de huertos, pozo de aguas vivas, que corren del Líbano.

verses.KJV: Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.
verses.WEB: Awake, north wind, and come, you south! Blow on my garden, that its spices may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and taste his precious fruits.
verses.ASV: Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; Blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, And eat his precious fruits.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Ela] : Levanta-te, vento norte! E vem, ó vento sul! Assopra em meu jardim, para que espalhem os seus aromas! Que meu amado venha a seu jardim, e coma de seus excelentes frutos.
verses.RVR09: Levántate, Aquilón, y ven, Austro: sopla mi huerto, despréndanse sus aromas. Venga mi amado á su huerto, y coma de su dulce fruta.

verses.KJV: I am come into my garden, my sister, my spouse: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk: eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved.
verses.WEB: I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Friends Eat, friends! Drink, yes, drink abundantly, beloved.
verses.ASV: I am come into my garden, my sister, [my] bride: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O friends; Drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Ele] : Já cheguei ao meu jardim, minha irmã, [minha] esposa; colhi minha mirra com minha especiaria; comi meu mel, bebi meu vinho com meu leite. [Autor do poema (ou os amigos dos noivos)] : Comei, amigos; bebei, ó amados, e embebedai-vos.
verses.RVR09: YO vine á mi huerto, oh hermana, esposa mía: cogido he mi mirra y mis aromas; he comido mi panal y mi miel, mi vino y mi leche he bebido. Comed, amigos; bebed, amados, y embriagaos.

verses.KJV: I sleep, but my heart waketh: it is the voice of my beloved that knocketh, saying, Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is filled with dew, and my locks with the drops of the night.
verses.WEB: I was asleep, but my heart was awake. It is the voice of my beloved who knocks: “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled; for my head is filled with dew, and my hair with the dampness of the night.”
verses.ASV: I was asleep, but my heart waked: It is the voice of my beloved that knocketh, [saying], Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled; For my head is filled with dew, My locks with the drops of the night.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Ela] : Eu estava dormindo, mas meu coração vigiava; era a voz de meu amado, batendo: Abre-me, minha irmã, minha querida, minha pomba, minha perfeita! Porque minha cabeça está cheia de orvalho, meus cabelos das gotas da noite.
verses.RVR09: Yo dormía, pero mi corazón velaba: la voz de mi amado que llamaba: Abreme, hermana mía, amiga mía, paloma mía, perfecta mía; porque mi cabeza está llena de rocío, mis cabellos de las gotas de la noche.

verses.KJV: I have put off my coat; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?
verses.WEB: I have taken off my robe. Indeed, must I put it on? I have washed my feet. Indeed, must I soil them?
verses.ASV: I have put off my garment; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?
verses.ALMEIDA: Já tirei minha roupa; como [voltarei] a vesti-la? Já lavei meus pés; como vou sujá-los [de novo] ?
verses.RVR09: Heme desnudado mi ropa; ¿cómo la tengo de vestir? He lavado mis pies; ¿cómo los tengo de ensuciar?

verses.KJV: My beloved put in his hand by the hole of the door, and my bowels were moved for him.
verses.WEB: My beloved thrust his hand in through the latch opening. My heart pounded for him.
verses.ASV: My beloved put in his hand by the hole [of the door], And my heart was moved for him.
verses.ALMEIDA: Meu amado meteu sua mão pelo buraco [da porta] ,e meu interior se estremeceu por ele.
verses.RVR09: Mi amado metió su mano por el agujero, y mis entrañas se conmovieron dentro de mí.

verses.KJV: I rose up to open to my beloved; and my hands dropped with myrrh, and my fingers with sweet smelling myrrh, upon the handles of the lock.
verses.WEB: I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with liquid myrrh, on the handles of the lock.
verses.ASV: I rose up to open to my beloved; And my hands dropped with myrrh, And my fingers with liquid myrrh, Upon the handles of the bolt.
verses.ALMEIDA: Eu me levantei para abrir a meu amado; minhas mãos gotejavam mirra, e meus dedos [derramaram] mirra sobre os puxadores da fechadura.
verses.RVR09: Yo me levanté para abrir á mi amado, y mis manos gotearon mirra, y mis dedos mirra que corría sobre las aldabas del candado.

verses.KJV: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved had withdrawn himself, and was gone: my soul failed when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.
verses.WEB: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved left, and had gone away. My heart went out when he spoke. I looked for him, but I didn’t find him. I called him, but he didn’t answer.
verses.ASV: I opened to my beloved; But my beloved had withdrawn himself, [and] was gone. My soul had failed me when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.
verses.ALMEIDA: Eu abri a porta ao meu amado, porém meu amado já tinha saído e ido embora; minha alma como que saía [de si] por causa de seu falar. Eu o busquei, mas não o achei; eu o chamei, mas ele não me respondeu.
verses.RVR09: Abrí yo á mi amado; mas mi amado se había ido, había ya pasado: y tras su hablar salió mi alma: busquélo, y no lo hallé; llamélo, y no me respondió.

verses.KJV: The watchmen that went about the city found me, they smote me, they wounded me; the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.
verses.WEB: The watchmen who go about the city found me. They beat me. They bruised me. The keepers of the walls took my cloak away from me.
verses.ASV: The watchmen that go about the city found me, They smote me, they wounded me; The keepers of the walls took away my mantle from me.
verses.ALMEIDA: Os guardas que rondavam pela cidade me encontraram; eles me bateram [e] me feriram; os guardas dos muros tiraram de mim o meu véu.
verses.RVR09: Halláronme los guardas que rondan la ciudad: hiriéronme, llagáronme, quitáronme mi manto de encima los guardas de los muros.

verses.KJV: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if ye find my beloved, that ye tell him, that I am sick of love.
verses.WEB: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, If you find my beloved, that you tell him that I am faint with love.
verses.ASV: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, If ye find my beloved, That ye tell him, that I am sick from love.
verses.ALMEIDA: Eu vos ordeno, filhas de Jerusalém: jurai que, se achardes o meu amado, dizei a ele que estou doente de amor.
verses.RVR09: Yo os conjuro, oh doncellas de Jerusalem, si hallareis á mi amado, que le hagáis saber como de amor estoy enferma.

verses.KJV: What is thy beloved more than another beloved, O thou fairest among women? what is thy beloved more than another beloved, that thou dost so charge us?
verses.WEB: How is your beloved better than another beloved, you fairest among women? How is your beloved better than another beloved, that you do so adjure us?
verses.ASV: What is thy beloved more than [another] beloved, O thou fairest among women? What is thy beloved more than [another] beloved, That thou dost so adjure us?
verses.ALMEIDA: [Moças] : Ó, tu, mais bela entre as mulheres, como é o teu amado, a quem tu amas mais do que qualquer outro? Como é este teu amado, mais amado que qualquer outro, por quem assim nos mandas jurar?
verses.RVR09: ¿Qué es tu amado más que otro amado, oh la más hermosa de todas las mujeres? ¿qué es tu amado más que otro amado, que así nos conjuras?

verses.KJV: My beloved is white and ruddy, the chiefest among ten thousand.
verses.WEB: My beloved is white and ruddy. The best among ten thousand.
verses.ASV: My beloved is white and ruddy, The chiefest among ten thousand.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Ela] : Meu amado é radiante e rosado; ele se destaca entre dez mil.
verses.RVR09: Mi amado es blanco y rubio, señalado entre diez mil.

verses.KJV: His head is as the most fine gold, his locks are bushy, and black as a raven.
verses.WEB: His head is like the purest gold. His hair is bushy, black as a raven.
verses.ASV: His head is [as] the most fine gold; His locks are bushy, [and] black as a raven.
verses.ALMEIDA: Sua cabeça é [como] o mais fino ouro; seus cabelos são crespos, pretos como o corvo.
verses.RVR09: Su cabeza, como oro finísimo; sus cabellos crespos, negros como el cuervo.

verses.KJV: His eyes are as the eyes of doves by the rivers of waters, washed with milk, and fitly set.
verses.WEB: His eyes are like doves beside the water brooks, washed with milk, mounted like jewels.
verses.ASV: His eyes are like doves beside the water-brooks, Washed with milk, [and] fitly set.
verses.ALMEIDA: Seus olhos são como pombas junto às correntes de águas, lavados em leite, colocados como [joias] .
verses.RVR09: Sus ojos, como palomas junto á los arroyos de las aguas, que se lavan con leche, y á la perfección colocados.

verses.KJV: His cheeks are as a bed of spices, as sweet flowers: his lips like lilies, dropping sweet smelling myrrh.
verses.WEB: His cheeks are like a bed of spices with towers of perfumes. His lips are like lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.
verses.ASV: His cheeks are as a bed of spices, [As] banks of sweet herbs: His lips are [as] lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.
verses.ALMEIDA: As laterais de seu rosto como um canteiro de especiarias, [como] caixas aromáticas; seus lábios são [como] lírios, que gotejam fragrante mirra.
verses.RVR09: Sus mejillas, como una era de especias aromáticas, como fragantes flores: sus labios, como lirios que destilan mirra que trasciende.

verses.KJV: His hands are as gold rings set with the beryl: his belly is as bright ivory overlaid with sapphires.
verses.WEB: His hands are like rings of gold set with beryl. His body is like ivory work overlaid with sapphires.
verses.ASV: His hands are [as] rings of gold set with beryl: His body is [as] ivory work overlaid [with] sapphires.
verses.ALMEIDA: Suas mãos são [como] anéis de ouro com pedras de crisólitos; seu abdome [como] o brilhante marfim, coberto de safiras.
verses.RVR09: Sus manos, como anillos de oro engastados de jacintos: su vientre, como claro marfil cubierto de zafiros.

verses.KJV: His legs are as pillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold: his countenance is as Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.
verses.WEB: His legs are like pillars of marble set on sockets of fine gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.
verses.ASV: His legs are [as] pillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold: His aspect is like Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.
verses.ALMEIDA: Suas pernas são [como] colunas de mármore, fundadas sobre bases de ouro puro; seu aspecto é como o Líbano, precioso como os cedros.
verses.RVR09: Sus piernas, como columnas de mármol fundadas sobre basas de fino oro: su aspecto como el Líbano, escogido como los cedros.

verses.KJV: His mouth is most sweet: yea, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.WEB: His mouth is sweetness; yes, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.ASV: His mouth is most sweet; Yea, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.ALMEIDA: Sua boca é [cheia] de doçura, e ele é desejável em todos os sentidos; assim é o meu amado; assim é o meu querido, ó filhas de Jerusalém.
verses.RVR09: Su paladar, dulcísimo: y todo él codiciable. Tal es mi amado, tal es mi amigo, oh doncellas de Jerusalem.

verses.KJV: Whither is thy beloved gone, O thou fairest among women? whither is thy beloved turned aside? that we may seek him with thee.
verses.WEB: Where has your beloved gone, you fairest among women? Where has your beloved turned, that we may seek him with you?
verses.ASV: Whither is thy beloved gone, O thou fairest among women? Whither hath thy beloved turned him, That we may seek him with thee?
verses.ALMEIDA: [Moças] : Para onde foi o teu amado, ó tu mais bela entre as mulheres? Para que direção se virou o teu amado, para o procurarmos contigo?
verses.RVR09: ¿DÓNDE se ha ido tu amado, oh la más hermosa de todas las mujeres? ¿Adónde se apartó tu amado, y le buscaremos contigo?

verses.KJV: My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices, to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
verses.WEB: My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to pasture his flock in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
verses.ASV: My beloved is gone down to his garden, To the beds of spices, To feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Ela] : Meu amado desceu ao seu jardim, aos canteiros de especiarias, para apascentar [seu rebanho] nos jardins, e para colher lírios.
verses.RVR09: Mi amado descendió á su huerto, á las eras de los aromas, para apacentar en los huertos, y para coger los lirios.

verses.KJV: I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine: he feedeth among the lilies.
verses.WEB: I am my beloved’s, and my beloved is mine. He browses among the lilies.
verses.ASV: I am my beloved’s, and my beloved is mine: He feedeth [his flock] among the lilies.
verses.ALMEIDA: Eu sou do meu amado, e meu amado é meu; ele apascenta entre os lírios.
verses.RVR09: Yo soy de mi amado, y mi amado es mío: él apacienta entre los lirios.

verses.KJV: Thou art beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah, comely as Jerusalem, terrible as an army with banners.
verses.WEB: You are beautiful, my love, as Tirzah, lovely as Jerusalem, awesome as an army with banners.
verses.ASV: Thou art fair, O my love, as Tirzah, Comely as Jerusalem, Terrible as an army with banners.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Ele] : Tu és bela, minha querida, como Tirza, agradável como Jerusalém; és formidável como bandeiras [de exércitos] .
verses.RVR09: Hermosa eres tú, oh amiga mía, como Tirsa; de desear, como Jerusalem; imponente como ejércitos en orden.

verses.KJV: Turn away thine eyes from me, for they have overcome me: thy hair is as a flock of goats that appear from Gilead.
verses.WEB: Turn away your eyes from me, for they have overcome me. Your hair is like a flock of goats, that lie along the side of Gilead.
verses.ASV: Turn away thine eyes from me, For they have overcome me. Thy hair is as a flock of goats, That lie along the side of Gilead.
verses.ALMEIDA: Afasta teus olhos de mim, pois eles me deixam desconcertado. Teu cabelo é como um rebanho de cabras, que descem de Gileade.
verses.RVR09: Aparta tus ojos de delante de mí, porque ellos me vencieron. Tu cabello es como manada de cabras, que se muestran en Galaad.

verses.KJV: Thy teeth are as a flock of sheep which go up from the washing, whereof every one beareth twins, and there is not one barren among them.
verses.WEB: Your teeth are like a flock of ewes, which have come up from the washing, of which every one has twins; not one is bereaved among them.
verses.ASV: Thy teeth are like a flock of ewes, Which are come up from the washing; Whereof every one hath twins, And none is bereaved among them.
verses.ALMEIDA: Teus dentes são como um rebanho de ovelhas, que sobem do lavatório; todas produzem gêmeos, e não há estéril entre elas.
verses.RVR09: Tus dientes, como manada de ovejas que suben del lavadero, todas con crías mellizas, y estéril no hay entre ellas.

verses.KJV: As a piece of a pomegranate are thy temples within thy locks.
verses.WEB: Your temples are like a piece of a pomegranate behind your veil.
verses.ASV: Thy temples are like a piece of a pomegranate Behind thy veil.
verses.ALMEIDA: Como um pedaço de romã, assim são as laterais de teu rosto abaixo de teu véu.
verses.RVR09: Como cachos de granada son tus sienes entre tus guedejas.

verses.KJV: There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, and virgins without number.
verses.WEB: There are sixty queens, eighty concubines, and virgins without number.
verses.ASV: There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, And virgins without number.
verses.ALMEIDA: Sessenta são as rainhas, e oitenta as concubinas; e as donzelas são inúmeras;
verses.RVR09: Sesenta son las reinas, y ochenta las concubinas, y las doncellas sin cuento:

verses.KJV: My dove, my undefiled is but one; she is the only one of her mother, she is the choice one of her that bare her. The daughters saw her, and blessed her; yea, the queens and the concubines, and they praised her.
verses.WEB: My dove, my perfect one, is unique. She is her mother’s only daughter. She is the favorite one of her who bore her. The daughters saw her, and called her blessed. The queens and the concubines saw her, and they praised her.
verses.ASV: My dove, my undefiled, is [but] one; She is the only one of her mother; She is the choice one of her that bare her. The daughters saw her, and called her blessed; [Yea], the queens and the concubines, and they praised her.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Porém] uma é a minha pomba, minha perfeita, a única de sua mãe, a mais querida daquela que a gerou. As moças a viram, e a chamaram de bem-aventurada; as rainhas e as concubinas a elogiaram.
verses.RVR09: Mas una es la paloma mía, la perfecta mía; única es á su madre, escogida á la que la engendró. Viéronla las doncellas, y llamáronla bienaventurada; las reinas y las concubinas, y la alabaron.

verses.KJV: Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners?
verses.WEB: Who is she who looks out as the morning, beautiful as the moon, clear as the sun, and awesome as an army with banners?
verses.ASV: Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, Fair as the moon, Clear as the sun, Terrible as an army with banners?
verses.ALMEIDA: Quem é esta, que aparece como o nascer do dia, bela como a lua, brilhante como o sol, formidável como bandeiras [de exércitos] ?
verses.RVR09: ¿Quién es ésta que se muestra como el alba, hermosa como la luna, esclarecida como el sol, imponente como ejércitos en orden?

verses.KJV: I went down into the garden of nuts to see the fruits of the valley, and to see whether the vine flourished and the pomegranates budded.
verses.WEB: I went down into the nut tree grove, to see the green plants of the valley, to see whether the vine budded, and the pomegranates were in flower.
verses.ASV: I went down into the garden of nuts, To see the green plants of the valley, To see whether the vine budded, [And] the pomegranates were in flower.
verses.ALMEIDA: Desci ao jardim das nogueiras, para ver os frutos do vale; para ver se as videiras estavam floridas, [e se] as romãzeiras brotavam.
verses.RVR09: Al huerto de los nogales descendí á ver los frutos del valle, y para ver si brotaban las vides, si florecían los granados.

verses.KJV: Or ever I was aware, my soul made me like the chariots of Amminadib.
verses.WEB: Without realizing it, my desire set me with my royal people’s chariots.
verses.ASV: Before I was aware, my soul set me [Among] the chariots of my princely people.
verses.ALMEIDA: Sem eu perceber, minha alma me pôs nas carruagens de meu nobre povo.
verses.RVR09: No lo supe: hame mi alma hecho como los carros de Amminadab.

verses.KJV: Return, return, O Shulamite; return, return, that we may look upon thee. What will ye see in the Shulamite? As it were the company of two armies.
verses.WEB: Return, return, Shulammite! Return, return, that we may gaze at you. Lover Why do you desire to gaze at the Shulammite, as at the dance of Mahanaim?
verses.ASV: Return, return, O Shulammite; Return, return, that we may look upon thee. Why will ye look upon the Shulammite, As upon the dance of Mahanaim?
verses.ALMEIDA: [Moças] : Volta! Volta, Sulamita! Volta! Volta, e nós te veremos! [Ele] : Por que [quereis] ver a Sulamita, como a dança de duas companhias?
verses.RVR09: Tórnate, tórnate, oh Sulamita; tórnate, tórnate, y te miraremos. ¿Qué veréis en la Sulamita? Como la reunión de dos campamentos.

verses.KJV: How beautiful are thy feet with shoes, O prince's daughter! the joints of thy thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a cunning workman.
verses.WEB: How beautiful are your feet in sandals, prince’s daughter! Your rounded thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a skillful workman.
verses.ASV: How beautiful are thy feet in sandals, O prince’s daughter! Thy rounded thighs are like jewels, The work of the hands of a skilful workman.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Ele] : Como são belos os teus pés nas sandálias, ó filha de príncipe! Os contornos de tuas coxas são como joias, [como] obra das mãos de um artesão.
verses.RVR09: ¡CUÁN hermosos son tus pies en los calzados, oh hija de príncipe! Los contornos de tus muslos son como joyas, obra de mano de excelente maestro.

verses.KJV: Thy navel is like a round goblet, which wanteth not liquor: thy belly is like an heap of wheat set about with lilies.
verses.WEB: Your body is like a round goblet, no mixed wine is wanting. Your waist is like a heap of wheat, set about with lilies.
verses.ASV: Thy body is [like] a round goblet, [Wherein] no mingled wine is wanting: Thy waist is [like] a heap of wheat Set about with lilies.
verses.ALMEIDA: Teu umbigo é [como] uma taça redonda, que não falta bebida; teu abdome é [como] um amontoado de trigo, rodeado de lírios.
verses.RVR09: Tu ombligo, como una taza redonda, que no le falta bebida. Tu vientre, como montón de trigo, cercado de lirios.

verses.KJV: Thy two breasts are like two young roes that are twins.
verses.WEB: Your two breasts are like two fawns, that are twins of a roe.
verses.ASV: Thy two breasts are like two fawns That are twins of a roe.
verses.ALMEIDA: Teus dois seios são como dois filhos gêmeos da corça.
verses.RVR09: Tus dos pechos, como dos cabritos mellizos de gama.

verses.KJV: Thy neck is as a tower of ivory; thine eyes like the fishpools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bathrabbim: thy nose is as the tower of Lebanon which looketh toward Damascus.
verses.WEB: Your neck is like an ivory tower. Your eyes are like the pools in Heshbon by the gate of Bathrabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon which looks toward Damascus.
verses.ASV: Thy neck is like the tower of ivory; Thine eyes [as] the pools in Heshbon, By the gate of Bath-rabbim; Thy nose is like the tower of Lebanon Which looketh toward Damascus.
verses.ALMEIDA: Teu pescoço é como uma torre de marfim; teus olhos são [como] os tanques de peixes de Hesbom, junto à porta de Bate-Rabim. Teu nariz é como a torre do Líbano, que está de frente a Damasco.
verses.RVR09: Tu cuello, como torre de marfil; tus ojos, como las pesqueras de Hesbón junto á la puerta de Batrabbim; tu nariz, como la torre del Líbano, que mira hacia Damasco.

verses.KJV: Thine head upon thee is like Carmel, and the hair of thine head like purple; the king is held in the galleries.
verses.WEB: Your head on you is like Carmel. The hair of your head like purple. The king is held captive in its tresses.
verses.ASV: Thy head upon thee is like Carmel, And the hair of thy head like purple; The king is held captive in the tresses [thereof].
verses.ALMEIDA: Tua cabeça sobre ti, como o [monte] Carmelo, e o trançado dos cabelos cabeça como púrpura; o rei está [como que] atado em [tuas] tranças.
verses.RVR09: Tu cabeza encima de ti, como el Carmelo; y el cabello de tu cabeza, como la púrpura del rey ligada en los corredores.

verses.KJV: How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!
verses.WEB: How beautiful and how pleasant you are, love, for delights!
verses.ASV: How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!
verses.ALMEIDA: Como tu és bela! Como tu és agradável, ó amor em delícias!
verses.RVR09: ¡Qué hermosa eres, y cuán suave, oh amor deleitoso!

verses.KJV: This thy stature is like to a palm tree, and thy breasts to clusters of grapes.
verses.WEB: This, your stature, is like a palm tree, your breasts like its fruit.
verses.ASV: This thy stature is like to a palm-tree, And thy breasts to its clusters.
verses.ALMEIDA: Esta tua estatura é semelhante à palmeira, e teus seios são [como] cachos [de uvas] .
verses.RVR09: ¡Y tu estatura es semejante á la palma, y tus pechos á los racimos!

verses.KJV: I said, I will go up to the palm tree, I will take hold of the boughs thereof: now also thy breasts shall be as clusters of the vine, and the smell of thy nose like apples;
verses.WEB: I said, “I will climb up into the palm tree. I will take hold of its fruit.” Let your breasts be like clusters of the vine, the smell of your breath like apples.
verses.ASV: I said, I will climb up into the palm-tree, I will take hold of the branches thereof: Let thy breasts be as clusters of the vine, And the smell of thy breath like apples,
verses.ALMEIDA: Eu disse: Subirei à palmeira, pegarei dos seus ramos; e então teus seios serão como os cachos da videira, e a fragrância de teu nariz como o das maçãs.
verses.RVR09: Yo dije: Subiré á la palma, asiré sus ramos: y tus pechos serán ahora como racimos de vid, y el olor de tu boca como de manzanas;

verses.KJV: And the roof of thy mouth like the best wine for my beloved, that goeth down sweetly, causing the lips of those that are asleep to speak.
verses.WEB: Your mouth is like the best wine, that goes down smoothly for my beloved, gliding through the lips of those who are asleep.
verses.ASV: And thy mouth like the best wine, That goeth down smoothly for my beloved, Gliding through the lips of those that are asleep.
verses.ALMEIDA: E tua boca [seja] como o bom vinho; [Ela] : [Vinho] que se entra a meu amado suavemente, e faz falarem os lábios dos que dormem.
verses.RVR09: Y tu paladar como el buen vino, que se entra á mi amado suavemente, y hace hablar los labios de los viejos.

verses.KJV: I am my beloved's, and his desire is toward me.
verses.WEB: I am my beloved’s. His desire is toward me.
verses.ASV: I am my beloved’s; And his desire is toward me.
verses.ALMEIDA: Eu sou do meu amado, e ele me deseja.
verses.RVR09: Yo soy de mi amado, y conmigo tiene su contentamiento.

verses.KJV: Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field; let us lodge in the villages.
