verses.KJV: And when it was told me how that the Jews laid wait for the man, I sent straightway to thee, and gave commandment to his accusers also to say before thee what they had against him. Farewell.
verses.WEB: When I was told that the Jews lay in wait for the man, I sent him to you immediately, charging his accusers also to bring their accusations against him before you. Farewell.”
verses.ASV: And when it was shown to me that there would be a plot against the man, I sent him to thee forthwith, charging his accusers also to speak against him before thee.
verses.ALMEIDA: E tendo sido avisado de que os judeus estavam para pôr uma cilada contra este homem, logo eu [o] enviei a ti, mandando também aos acusadores que diante de ti digam o que [tiverem] contra ele. Que tu estejas bem.
verses.RVR09: Mas siéndome dado aviso de asechanzas que le habían aparejado los Judíos, luego al punto le he enviado á ti, intimando también á los acusadores que traten delante de ti lo que tienen contra él. Pásalo bien.

verses.KJV: Then the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul, and brought him by night to Antipatris.
verses.WEB: So the soldiers, carrying out their orders, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.
verses.ASV: So the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.
verses.ALMEIDA: Tendo então os soldados tomado a Paulo, assim como lhes tinha sido ordenado, trouxeram-no durante a noite a Antipátride.
verses.RVR09: Y los soldados, tomando á Pablo como les era mandado, lleváronle de noche á Antipatris.

verses.KJV: On the morrow they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle:
verses.WEB: But on the next day they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the barracks.
verses.ASV: But on the morrow they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle:
verses.ALMEIDA: E no [dia] seguinte, deixando irem com ele os cavaleiros, voltaram à área fortificada.
verses.RVR09: Y al día siguiente, dejando á los de á caballo que fuesen con él, se volvieron á la fortaleza.

verses.KJV: Who, when they came to Caesarea and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him.
verses.WEB: When they came to Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor, they also presented Paul to him.
verses.ASV: and they, when they came to Cæsarea and delivered the letter to the governor, presented Paul also before him.
verses.ALMEIDA: Os quais, tendo chegado a Cesareia, e entregado a carta ao governador, apresentaram-lhe também a Paulo.
verses.RVR09: Y como llegaron á Cesarea, y dieron la carta al gobernador, presentaron también á Pablo delante de él.

verses.KJV: And when the governor had read the letter, he asked of what province he was. And when he understood that he was of Cilicia;
verses.WEB: When the governor had read it, he asked what province he was from. When he understood that he was from Cilicia, he said,
verses.ASV: And when he had read it, he asked of what province he was; and when he understood that he was of Cilicia,
verses.ALMEIDA: E o governador, tendo lido [a carta] , perguntou de que província ele era; e ao entender que [era] da Cilícia,
verses.RVR09: Y el gobernador, leída la carta, preguntó de qué provincia era; y entendiendo que de Cilicia,

verses.KJV: I will hear thee, said he, when thine accusers are also come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod's judgment hall.
verses.WEB: “I will hear you fully when your accusers also arrive.” He commanded that he be kept in Herod’s palace.
verses.ASV: I will hear thee fully, said he, when thine accusers also are come: and he commanded him to be kept in Herod’s palace.
verses.ALMEIDA: disse: “Eu te ouvirei quando também chegarem os teus acusadores”. E mandou que o guardassem no palácio de Herodes.
verses.RVR09: Te oiré, dijo, cuando vinieren tus acusadores. Y mandó que le guardasen en el pretorio de Herodes.

verses.KJV: And after five days Ananias the high priest descended with the elders, and with a certain orator named Tertullus, who informed the governor against Paul.
verses.WEB: After five days, the high priest, Ananias, came down with certain elders and an orator, one Tertullus. They informed the governor against Paul.
verses.ASV: And after five days the high priest Ananias came down with certain elders, and [with] an orator, one Tertullus; and they informed the governor against Paul.
verses.ALMEIDA: E cinco dias depois, desceu o sumo sacerdote Ananias, com os anciãos e um certo orador Tértulo; os quais compareceram diante do governador contra Paulo.
verses.RVR09: Y CINCO días después descendió el sumo sacerdote Ananías, con algunos de los ancianos, y un cierto Tértulo, orador; y parecieron delante del gobernador contra Pablo.

verses.KJV: And when he was called forth, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, Seeing that by thee we enjoy great quietness, and that very worthy deeds are done unto this nation by thy providence,
verses.WEB: When he was called, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, “Seeing that by you we enjoy much peace, and that prosperity is coming to this nation by your foresight,
verses.ASV: And when he was called, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, Seeing that by thee we enjoy much peace, and that by thy providence evils are corrected for this nation,
verses.ALMEIDA: E sendo chamado, Tértulo começou a acusá [-lo] , dizendo:
verses.RVR09: Y citado que fué, Tértulo comenzó á acusar, diciendo: Como por causa tuya vivamos en grande paz, y muchas cosas sean bien gobernadas en el pueblo por tu prudencia,

verses.KJV: We accept it always, and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness.
verses.WEB: we accept it in all ways and in all places, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.
verses.ASV: we accept it in all ways and in all places, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Visto que] há muita paz por causa de ti, e que por teu governo muitos bons serviços estão sendo feitos a esta nação, excelentíssimo Félix, totalmente e em todo lugar, com todo agradecimento o reconhecemos.
verses.RVR09: Siempre y en todo lugar lo recibimos con todo hacimiento de gracias, oh excelentísimo Félix.

verses.KJV: Notwithstanding, that I be not further tedious unto thee, I pray thee that thou wouldest hear us of thy clemency a few words.
verses.WEB: But that I don’t delay you, I entreat you to bear with us and hear a few words.
verses.ASV: But, that I be not further tedious unto thee, I entreat thee to hear us of thy clemency a few words.
verses.ALMEIDA: Mas para que eu não gaste muito o teu tempo, rogo [-te] que tu nos ouças brevemente, conforme a tua clemência.
verses.RVR09: Empero por no molestarte más largamente, ruégote que nos oigas brevemente conforme á tu equidad.

verses.KJV: For we have found this man a pestilent fellow, and a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes:
verses.WEB: For we have found this man to be a plague, an instigator of insurrections among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes.
verses.ASV: For we have found this man a pestilent fellow, and a mover of insurrections among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes:
verses.ALMEIDA: Porque nós temos achado que este homem [é] uma peste, e levantador de rebeliões entre todos os judeus pelo mundo, e o principal defensor da seita dos nazarenos.
verses.RVR09: Porque hemos hallado que este hombre es pestilencial, y levantador de sediciones entre todos los Judíos por todo el mundo, y príncipe de la secta de los Nazarenos:

verses.KJV: Who also hath gone about to profane the temple: whom we took, and would have judged according to our law.
verses.WEB: He even tried to profane the temple, and we arrested him.
verses.ASV: who moreover assayed to profane the temple: on whom also we laid hold:
verses.ALMEIDA: O qual também tentou profanar o Templo; ao qual também prendemos, e quisemos julgar conforme a nossa Lei.
verses.RVR09: El cual también tentó á violar el templo; y prendiéndole, le quisimos juzgar conforme á nuestra ley:

verses.KJV: But the chief captain Lysias came upon us, and with great violence took him away out of our hands,
verses.WEB: By examining him yourself you may ascertain all these things of which we accuse him.”
verses.ASV: from whom thou wilt be able, by examining him thyself, to take knowledge of all these things whereof we accuse him.
verses.ALMEIDA: Mas tendo vindo sobre [nós] o comandante Lísias, com grande violência, tirou [-o] das nossas mãos;
verses.RVR09: Mas interviniendo el tribuno Lisias, con grande violencia le quitó de nuestras manos,

verses.KJV: Commanding his accusers to come unto thee: by examining of whom thyself mayest take knowledge of all these things, whereof we accuse him.
verses.WEB: The Jews also joined in the attack, affirming that these things were so.
verses.ASV: And the Jews also joined in the charge, affirming that these things were so.
verses.ALMEIDA: investigando-o tu mesmo, poderás entender todas estas coisas das quais o acusamos.
verses.RVR09: Mandando á sus acusadores que viniesen á ti; del cual tú mismo juzgando, podrás entender todas estas cosas de que le acusamos.

verses.KJV: And the Jews also assented, saying that these things were so.
verses.WEB: When the governor had beckoned to him to speak, Paul answered, “Because I know that you have been a judge of this nation for many years, I cheerfully make my defense,
verses.ASV: And when the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, Paul answered, Forasmuch as I know that thou hast been of many years a judge unto this nation, I cheerfully make my defence:
verses.ALMEIDA: E os judeus também concordaram, dizendo serem estas coisas assim.
verses.RVR09: Y contendían también los Judíos, diciendo ser así estas cosas.

verses.KJV: Then Paul, after that the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, answered, Forasmuch as I know that thou hast been of many years a judge unto this nation, I do the more cheerfully answer for myself:
verses.WEB: seeing that you can verify that it is not more than twelve days since I went up to worship at Jerusalem.
verses.ASV: seeing that thou canst take knowledge that it is not more than twelve days since I went up to worship at Jerusalem:
verses.ALMEIDA: Mas Paulo, fazendo gesto ao governador para que falasse, respondeu: Sabendo eu que por muitos anos tu tens sido juiz desta nação, com maior ânimo eu me defendo.
verses.RVR09: Entonces Pablo, haciéndole el gobernador señal que hablase, respondió: Porque sé que muchos años ha eres gobernador de esta nación, con buen ánimo satisfaré por mí.

verses.KJV: Because that thou mayest understand, that there are yet but twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem for to worship.
verses.WEB: In the temple they didn’t find me disputing with anyone or stirring up a crowd, either in the synagogues or in the city.
verses.ASV: and neither in the temple did they find me disputing with any man or stirring up a crowd, nor in the synagogues, nor in the city.
verses.ALMEIDA: Pois tu podes entender que há não mais que doze dias, eu tinha subido a Jerusalém para adorar.
verses.RVR09: Porque tú puedes entender que no hace más de doce días que subí á adorar á Jerusalem;

verses.KJV: And they neither found me in the temple disputing with any man, neither raising up the people, neither in the synagogues, nor in the city:
verses.WEB: Nor can they prove to you the things of which they now accuse me.
verses.ASV: Neither can they prove to thee the things whereof they now accuse me.
verses.ALMEIDA: E nem me acharam falando com alguém no Templo, nem incitando ao povo, nem nas sinagogas, nem na cidade.
verses.RVR09: Y ni me hallaron en el templo disputando con ninguno, ni haciendo concurso de multitud, ni en sinagogas, ni en la ciudad;

verses.KJV: Neither can they prove the things whereof they now accuse me.
verses.WEB: But this I confess to you, that according to the Way, which they call a sect, so I serve the God of our fathers, believing all things which are according to the law, and which are written in the prophets;
verses.ASV: But this I confess unto thee, that after the Way which they call a sect, so serve I the God of our fathers, believing all things which are according to the law, and which are written in the prophets;
verses.ALMEIDA: E nem podem provar as coisas das quais agora estão me acusando.
verses.RVR09: Ni te pueden probar las cosas de que ahora me acusan.

verses.KJV: But this I confess unto thee, that after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets:
verses.WEB: having hope toward God, which these also themselves look for, that there will be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.
verses.ASV: having hope toward God, which these also themselves look for, that there shall be a resurrection both of the just and unjust.
verses.ALMEIDA: Mas isto eu te confesso, que conforme o Caminho que eles chamam de seita, assim eu sirvo ao Deus dos [meus] pais, crendo em tudo que está escrito na Lei e nos profetas;
verses.RVR09: Esto empero te confieso, que conforme á aquel Camino que llaman herejía, así sirvo al Dios de mis padres, creyendo todas las cosas que en la ley y en los profetas están escritas;

verses.KJV: And have hope toward God, which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.
verses.WEB: In this I also practice always having a conscience void of offense toward God and men.
verses.ASV: Herein I also exercise myself to have a conscience void of offence toward God and men always.
verses.ALMEIDA: Tendo esperança em Deus, ao qual estes mesmos também esperam, que vai haver ressurreição dos mortos, tanto dos justos como dos injustos.
verses.RVR09: Teniendo esperanza en Dios que ha de haber resurrección de los muertos, así de justos como de injustos, la cual también ellos esperan.

verses.KJV: And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void to offence toward God, and toward men.
verses.WEB: Now after some years, I came to bring gifts for the needy to my nation, and offerings;
verses.ASV: Now after some years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings:
verses.ALMEIDA: E nisto eu pratico, [em que] tanto para com Deus como para com os seres humanos eu sempre tenha uma consciência limpa.
verses.RVR09: Y por esto, procuro yo tener siempre conciencia sin remordimiento acerca de Dios y acerca de los hombres.

verses.KJV: Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.
verses.WEB: amid which certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, not with a mob, nor with turmoil.
verses.ASV: amidst which they found me purified in the temple, with no crowd, nor yet with tumult: but [there were] certain Jews from Asia—
verses.ALMEIDA: E muitos anos depois, vim para fazer doações e ofertas à minha nação.
verses.RVR09: Mas pasados muchos años, vine á hacer limosnas á mi nación, y ofrendas,

verses.KJV: Whereupon certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither with multitude, nor with tumult.
verses.WEB: They ought to have been here before you and to make accusation if they had anything against me.
verses.ASV: who ought to have been here before thee, and to make accusation, if they had aught against me.
verses.ALMEIDA: Nisto, tendo eu me purificado, nem com multidões, nem com tumulto, alguns judeus da Ásia me acharam,
verses.RVR09: Cuando me hallaron purificado en el templo (no con multitud ni con alboroto) unos Judíos de Asia;

verses.KJV: Who ought to have been here before thee, and object, if they had ought against me.
verses.WEB: Or else let these men themselves say what injustice they found in me when I stood before the council,
verses.ASV: Or else let these men themselves say what wrong-doing they found when I stood before the council,
verses.ALMEIDA: Os quais era necessário que estivessem [aqui] presentes diante de ti, se tivessem alguma coisa contra mim.
verses.RVR09: Los cuales debieron comparecer delante de ti, y acusarme, si contra mí tenían algo.

verses.KJV: Or else let these same here say, if they have found any evil doing in me, while I stood before the council,
verses.WEB: unless it is for this one thing that I cried standing among them, ‘Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am being judged before you today!’”
verses.ASV: except it be for this one voice, that I cried standing among them, Touching the resurrection of the dead I am called in question before you this day.
verses.ALMEIDA: Ou digam estes mesmos, se eles acharam alguma má ação em mim quando eu estava perante o supremo conselho;
verses.RVR09: O digan estos mismos si hallaron en mí alguna cosa mal hecha, cuando yo estuve en el concilio,

verses.KJV: Except it be for this one voice, that I cried standing among them, Touching the resurrection of the dead I am called in question by you this day.
verses.WEB: But Felix, having more exact knowledge concerning the Way, deferred them, saying, “When Lysias, the commanding officer, comes down, I will decide your case.”
verses.ASV: But Felix, having more exact knowledge concerning the Way, deferred them, saying, When Lysias the chief captain shall come down, I will determine your matter.
verses.ALMEIDA: A não ser somente esta palavra com que, quando eu estava entre eles, clamei, que pela ressurreição dos mortos eu estou sendo julgado hoje por vós.
verses.RVR09: Si no sea que, estando entre ellos prorrumpí en alta voz: Acerca de la resurrección de los muertos soy hoy juzgado de vosotros.

verses.KJV: And when Felix heard these things, having more perfect knowledge of that way, he deferred them, and said, When Lysias the chief captain shall come down, I will know the uttermost of your matter.
verses.WEB: He ordered the centurion that Paul should be kept in custody and should have some privileges, and not to forbid any of his friends to serve him or to visit him.
verses.ASV: And he gave order to the centurion that he should be kept in charge, and should have indulgence; and not to forbid any of his friends to minister unto him.
verses.ALMEIDA: Tendo ouvido estas coisas, Félix, que sabia mais detalhadamente sobre o Caminho, adiou-lhes, dizendo: Quando o comandante Lísias descer, eu procurarei saber melhor de vossos assuntos.
verses.RVR09: Entonces Félix, oídas estas cosas, estando bien informado de esta secta, les puso dilación, diciendo: Cuando descendiere el tribuno Lisias acabaré de conocer de vuestro negocio.

verses.KJV: And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul, and to let him have liberty, and that he should forbid none of his acquaintance to minister or come unto him.
verses.WEB: After some days, Felix came with Drusilla his wife, who was a Jewess, and sent for Paul and heard him concerning the faith in Christ Jesus.
verses.ASV: But after certain days, Felix came with Drusilla, his wife, who was a Jewess, and sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ Jesus.
verses.ALMEIDA: E ele mandou ao centurião que guardassem a Paulo, e estivesse com [alguma] liberdade, e impedir a ninguém dos seus [amigos] lhe prestasse serviço, ou vir até ele.
verses.RVR09: Y mandó al centurión que Pablo fuese guardado, y aliviado de las prisiones; y que no vedase á ninguno de sus familiares servirle, ó venir á él.

verses.KJV: And after certain days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, which was a Jewess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.
verses.WEB: As he reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was terrified, and answered, “Go your way for this time, and when it is convenient for me, I will summon you.”
verses.ASV: And as he reasoned of righteousness, and self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was terrified, and answered, Go thy way for this time; and when I have a convenient season, I will call thee unto me.
verses.ALMEIDA: E alguns dias depois, tendo vindo Félix com a mulher dele Drusila, que era judia, mandou chamar a Paulo, e o ouviu sobre a fé em Cristo.
verses.RVR09: Y algunos días después, viniendo Félix con Drusila, su mujer, la cual era Judía, llamó á Pablo, y oyó de él la fe que es en Jesucristo.

verses.KJV: And as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee.
verses.WEB: Meanwhile, he also hoped that money would be given to him by Paul, that he might release him. Therefore also he sent for him more often and talked with him.
verses.ASV: He hoped withal that money would be given him of Paul: wherefore also he sent for him the oftener, and communed with him.
verses.ALMEIDA: E ele, tendo discursado sobre a justiça, o domínio próprio, e o julgamento que está por vir, Félix temeu, [e] respondeu: Por agora vai; e tendo [outra] oportunidade, eu te chamarei.
verses.RVR09: Y disertando él de la justicia, y de la continencia, y del juicio venidero, espantado Félix, respondió: Ahora vete; mas en teniendo oportunidad te llamaré:

verses.KJV: He hoped also that money should have been given him of Paul, that he might loose him: wherefore he sent for him the oftener, and communed with him.
verses.WEB: But when two years were fulfilled, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus, and desiring to gain favor with the Jews, Felix left Paul in bonds.
verses.ASV: But when two years were fulfilled, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus; and desiring to gain favor with the Jews, Felix left Paul in bonds.
verses.ALMEIDA: Ele também esperava que lhe fosse dado [algum] dinheiro por Paulo, para que o soltasse; por isso ele também muitas vezes o mandava chamar, e conversava com ele.
verses.RVR09: Esperando también con esto, que de parte de Pablo le serían dados dineros, porque le soltase; por lo cual, haciéndole venir muchas veces, hablaba con él.

verses.KJV: But after two years Porcius Festus came into Felix' room: and Felix, willing to shew the Jews a pleasure, left Paul bound.
verses.ALMEIDA: Mas tendo completado dois anos, Félix teve por sucessor a Pórcio Festo. E Félix, querendo agradar dos judeus, deixou Paulo preso.
verses.RVR09: Mas al cabo de dos años recibió Félix por sucesor á Porcio Festo: y queriendo Félix ganar la gracia de los Judíos, dejó preso á Pablo.

verses.KJV: Now when Festus was come into the province, after three days he ascended from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
verses.WEB: Festus therefore, having come into the province, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.
verses.ASV: Festus therefore, having come into the province, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Cæsarea.
verses.ALMEIDA: Então Festo, tendo entrado na província, subiu dali três dias depois de Cesareia a Jerusalém.
verses.RVR09: FESTO pues, entrado en la provincia, tres días después subió de Cesarea á Jerusalem.

verses.KJV: Then the high priest and the chief of the Jews informed him against Paul, and besought him,
verses.WEB: Then the high priest and the principal men of the Jews informed him against Paul, and they begged him,
verses.ASV: And the chief priests and the principal men of the Jews informed him against Paul; and they besought him,
verses.ALMEIDA: E o sumo sacerdote e os líderes dos judeus compareceram diante dele contra Paulo, e lhe rogaram;
verses.RVR09: Y vinieron á él los príncipes de los sacerdotes y los principales de los Judíos contra Pablo; y le rogaron,

verses.KJV: And desired favour against him, that he would send for him to Jerusalem, laying wait in the way to kill him.
verses.WEB: asking a favor against him, that he would summon him to Jerusalem, plotting to kill him on the way.
verses.ASV: asking a favor against him, that he would send for him to Jerusalem; laying a plot to kill him on the way.
verses.ALMEIDA: Pedindo favor contra ele, para que o fizesse vir a Jerusalém, preparando cilada para o matarem no caminho.
verses.RVR09: Pidiendo gracia contra él, que le hiciese traer á Jerusalem, poniendo ellos asechanzas para matarle en el camino.

verses.KJV: But Festus answered, that Paul should be kept at Caesarea, and that he himself would depart shortly thither.
verses.WEB: However Festus answered that Paul should be kept in custody at Caesarea, and that he himself was about to depart shortly.
verses.ASV: Howbeit Festus answered, that Paul was kept in charge at Cæsarea, and that he himself was about to depart [thither] shortly.
verses.ALMEIDA: Mas Festo respondeu que Paulo estava guardado em Cesareia, e que ele logo estava indo [para lá] .
verses.RVR09: Mas Festo respondió, que Pablo estaba guardado en Cesarea, y que él mismo partiría presto.

verses.KJV: Let them therefore, said he, which among you are able, go down with me, and accuse this man, if there be any wickedness in him.
verses.WEB: “Let them therefore”, he said, “that are in power among you go down with me, and if there is anything wrong in the man, let them accuse him.”
verses.ASV: Let them therefore, saith he, that are of power among you go down with me, and if there is anything amiss in the man, let them accuse him.
verses.ALMEIDA: Ele disse: Então aqueles dentre vós que podem, desçam com [igo] , e se houver alguma coisa errada neste homem, acusem-no.
verses.RVR09: Los que de vosotros pueden, dijo, desciendan juntamente; y si hay algún crimen en este varón, acúsenle.

verses.KJV: And when he had tarried among them more than ten days, he went down unto Caesarea; and the next day sitting on the judgment seat commanded Paul to be brought.
verses.WEB: When he had stayed among them more than ten days, he went down to Caesarea, and on the next day he sat on the judgment seat, and commanded Paul to be brought.
verses.ASV: And when he had tarried among them not more than eight or ten days, he went down unto Cæsarea; and on the morrow he sat on the judgment-seat, and commanded Paul to be brought.
verses.ALMEIDA: E ele, tendo ficado entre eles mais de dez dias, desceu a Cesareia; e tendo se sentado no tribunal no [dia] seguinte, mandou que trouxessem a Paulo.
verses.RVR09: Y deteniéndose entre ellos no más de ocho ó diez días, venido á Cesarea, el siguiente día se sentó en el tribunal, y mandó que Pablo fuese traído.

verses.KJV: And when he was come, the Jews which came down from Jerusalem stood round about, and laid many and grievous complaints against Paul, which they could not prove.
verses.WEB: When he had come, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing against him many and grievous charges which they could not prove,
verses.ASV: And when he was come, the Jews that had come down from Jerusalem stood round about him, bringing against him many and grievous charges which they could not prove;
verses.ALMEIDA: E tendo ele vindo, os judeus que haviam descido de Jerusalém [o] rodearam, trazendo contra Paulo muitas e graves acusações, que não podiam provar.
verses.RVR09: El cual venido, le rodearon los Judíos que habían venido de Jerusalem, poniendo contra Pablo muchas y graves acusaciones, las cuales no podían probar;

verses.KJV: While he answered for himself, Neither against the law of the Jews, neither against the temple, nor yet against Caesar, have I offended any thing at all.
verses.WEB: while he said in his defense, “Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar, have I sinned at all.”
verses.ASV: while Paul said in his defence, Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Cæsar, have I sinned at all.
verses.ALMEIDA: Ele, disse em sua defesa: Eu não pequei nem contra a Lei dos judeus, nem contra o Templo, nem contra César, em coisa alguma.
verses.RVR09: Alegando él por su parte: Ni contra la ley de los Judíos, ni contra el templo, ni contra César he pecado en nada.

verses.KJV: But Festus, willing to do the Jews a pleasure, answered Paul, and said, Wilt thou go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these things before me?
verses.WEB: But Festus, desiring to gain favor with the Jews, answered Paul and said, “Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem and be judged by me there concerning these things?”
verses.ASV: But Festus, desiring to gain favor with the Jews, answered Paul and said, Wilt thou go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these things before me?
verses.ALMEIDA: Mas Festo, querendo agradar aos judeus, respondendo a Paulo, disse: Tu queres subir a Jerusalém e ser julgado sobre estas coisas diante de mim?
verses.RVR09: Mas Festo, queriendo congraciarse con los Judíos, respondiendo á Pablo, dijo: ¿Quieres subir á Jerusalem, y allá ser juzgado de estas cosas delante de mí?

verses.KJV: Then said Paul, I stand at Caesar's judgment seat, where I ought to be judged: to the Jews have I done no wrong, as thou very well knowest.
verses.WEB: But Paul said, “I am standing before Caesar’s judgment seat, where I ought to be tried. I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you also know very well.
verses.ASV: But Paul said, I am standing before Cæsar’s judgment-seat, where I ought to be judged: to the Jews have I done no wrong, as thou also very well knowest.
verses.ALMEIDA: E Paulo disse: Eu estou diante do tribunal de César, onde eu tenho que ser julgado; a nenhum dos judeus eu fiz mal, assim como também tu sabes muito bem.
verses.RVR09: Y Pablo dijo: Ante el tribunal de César estoy, donde conviene que sea juzgado. A los Judíos no he hecho injuria ninguna, como tú sabes muy bien.

verses.KJV: For if I be an offender, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Caesar.
verses.WEB: For if I have done wrong and have committed anything worthy of death, I don’t refuse to die; but if none of those things is true that they accuse me of, no one can give me up to them. I appeal to Caesar!”
verses.ASV: If then I am a wrong-doer, and have committed anything worthy of death, I refuse not to die; but if none of those things is [true] whereof these accuse me, no man can give me up unto them. I appeal unto Cæsar.
verses.ALMEIDA: Porque se eu fiz algum mal, ou cometi algo digno de morte, eu não recuso morrer; mas se nada há das coisas que este me acusam, ninguém pode me entregar a eles. Eu apelo a César.
verses.RVR09: Porque si alguna injuria, ó cosa alguna digna de muerte he hecho, no rehuso morir; mas si nada hay de las cosas de que éstos me acusan, nadie puede darme á ellos. A César apelo.

verses.KJV: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Hast thou appealed unto Caesar? unto Caesar shalt thou go.
verses.WEB: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, “You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you shall go.”
verses.ASV: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Thou hast appealed unto Cæsar: unto Cæsar shalt thou go.
verses.ALMEIDA: Então Paulo, tendo conversado com o Conselho, respondeu: Tu apelaste a César; a César irás.
verses.RVR09: Entonces Festo, habiendo hablado con el consejo, respondió: ¿A César has apelado? á César irás.

verses.KJV: And after certain days king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Caesarea to salute Festus.
verses.WEB: Now when some days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea and greeted Festus.
verses.ASV: Now when certain days were passed, Agrippa the king and Bernice arrived at Cæsarea, and saluted Festus.
verses.ALMEIDA: E passados alguns dias, o Rei Agripa e Berenice vieram a Cesareia para saudar a Festo.
verses.RVR09: Y pasados algunos días, el rey Agripa y Bernice vinieron á Cesarea á saludar á Festo.

verses.KJV: And when they had been there many days, Festus declared Paul's cause unto the king, saying, There is a certain man left in bonds by Felix:
verses.WEB: As he stayed there many days, Festus laid Paul’s case before the king, saying, “There is a certain man left a prisoner by Felix;
verses.ASV: And as they tarried there many days, Festus laid Paul’s case before the king, saying, There is a certain man left a prisoner by Felix;
verses.ALMEIDA: E quando tinham ficado ali muitos dias, Festo contou ao rei os assuntos de Paulo, dizendo: Um certo homem foi deixado [aqui] preso por Félix;
verses.RVR09: Y como estuvieron allí muchos días, Festo declaró la causa de Pablo al rey, diciendo: Un hombre ha sido dejado preso por Félix,

verses.KJV: About whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me, desiring to have judgment against him.
verses.WEB: about whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me, asking for a sentence against him.
verses.ASV: about whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed [me], asking for sentence against him.
verses.ALMEIDA: Por causa do qual, estando eu em Jerusalém, os chefes dos sacerdotes e os anciãos dos judeus compareceram [a mim] , pedindo julgamento contra ele.
verses.RVR09: Sobre el cual, cuando fuí á Jerusalem, vinieron á mí los príncipes de los sacerdotes y los ancianos de los Judíos, pidiendo condenación contra él:

verses.KJV: To whom I answered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die, before that he which is accused have the accusers face to face, and have licence to answer for himself concerning the crime laid against him.
verses.WEB: I answered them that it is not the custom of the Romans to give up any man to destruction before the accused has met the accusers face to face and has had opportunity to make his defense concerning the matter laid against him.
verses.ASV: To whom I answered, that it is not the custom of the Romans to give up any man, before that the accused have the accusers face to face, and have had opportunity to make his defence concerning the matter laid against him.
verses.ALMEIDA: Aos quais eu respondi não ser costume dos romanos entregar a algum homem à morte, antes que o acusado tenha seus acusadores face a face, e tenha oportunidade para se defender da acusação.
verses.RVR09: A los cuales respondí, no ser costumbre de los Romanos dar alguno á la muerte antes que el que es acusado tenga presentes sus acusadores, y haya lugar de defenderse de la acusación.

verses.KJV: Therefore, when they were come hither, without any delay on the morrow I sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought forth.
verses.WEB: When therefore they had come together here, I didn’t delay, but on the next day sat on the judgment seat and commanded the man to be brought.
verses.ASV: When therefore they were come together here, I made no delay, but on the next day sat on the judgment-seat, and commanded the man to be brought.
verses.ALMEIDA: Portanto, tendo eles se reunido aqui, fazendo nenhum adiamento, no [dia] seguinte, estando eu sentado no tribunal, mandei trazer ao homem.
verses.RVR09: Así que, habiendo venido ellos juntos acá, sin ninguna dilación, al día siguiente, sentado en el tribunal, mandé traer al hombre;

verses.KJV: Against whom when the accusers stood up, they brought none accusation of such things as I supposed:
verses.WEB: When the accusers stood up, they brought no charges against him of such things as I supposed;
verses.ASV: Concerning whom, when the accusers stood up, they brought no charge of such evil things as I supposed;
verses.ALMEIDA: Do qual os acusadores estando [aqui] presentes, trouxeram como acusação nenhuma das coisas que eu suspeitava.
verses.RVR09: Y estando presentes los acusadores, ningún cargo produjeron de los que yo sospechaba:

verses.KJV: But had certain questions against him of their own superstition, and of one Jesus, which was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
verses.WEB: but had certain questions against him about their own religion and about one Jesus, who was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
verses.ASV: but had certain questions against him of their own religion, and of one Jesus, who was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
verses.ALMEIDA: Mas tinham contra ele algumas questões relativas às próprias crenças deles, e de um certo morto Jesus, o qual Paulo afirmava estar vivo.
verses.RVR09: Solamente tenían contra él ciertas cuestiones acerca de su superstición, y de un cierto Jesús, difunto, el cual Pablo afirmaba que estaba vivo.

verses.KJV: And because I doubted of such manner of questions, I asked him whether he would go to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these matters.
verses.WEB: Being perplexed how to inquire concerning these things, I asked whether he was willing to go to Jerusalem and there be judged concerning these matters.
verses.ASV: And I, being perplexed how to inquire concerning these things, asked whether he would go to Jerusalem and there be judged of these matters.
verses.ALMEIDA: E eu, estando em duvida sobre [como] interrogar esta causa, disse, [perguntando] se ele queria ir a Jerusalém, e lá ser julgado sobre estas coisas.
verses.RVR09: Y yo, dudando en cuestión semejante, dije, si quería ir á Jerusalem, y allá ser juzgado de estas cosas.

verses.KJV: But when Paul had appealed to be reserved unto the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Caesar.
verses.WEB: But when Paul had appealed to be kept for the decision of the emperor, I commanded him to be kept until I could send him to Caesar.”
verses.ASV: But when Paul had appealed to be kept for the decision of the emperor, I commanded him to be kept till I should send him to Cæsar.
verses.ALMEIDA: Porém Paulo, tendo apelado para ser guardado ao interrogatório do imperador, mandei que o guardassem, até que eu o enviasse a César.
verses.RVR09: Mas apelando Pablo á ser guardado al conocimiento de Augusto, mandé que le guardasen hasta que le enviara á César.

verses.KJV: Then Agrippa said unto Festus, I would also hear the man myself. To morrow, said he, thou shalt hear him.
verses.WEB: Agrippa said to Festus, “I also would like to hear the man myself.” “Tomorrow,” he said, “you shall hear him.”
verses.ASV: And Agrippa [said] unto Festus, I also could wish to hear the man myself. To-morrow, saith he, thou shalt hear him.
verses.ALMEIDA: E Agripa disse a Festo: Eu também queria ouvir a este homem.E ele disse: E amanhã tu o ouvirás.
verses.RVR09: Entonces Agripa dijo á Festo: Yo también quisiera oir á ese hombre. Y él dijo: Mañana le oirás.

verses.KJV: And on the morrow, when Agrippa was come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and was entered into the place of hearing, with the chief captains, and principal men of the city, at Festus' commandment Paul was brought forth.
verses.WEB: So on the next day, when Agrippa and Bernice had come with great pomp, and they had entered into the place of hearing with the commanding officers and the principal men of the city, at the command of Festus, Paul was brought in.
verses.ASV: So on the morrow, when Agrippa was come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and they were entered into the place of hearing with the chief captains and the principal men of the city, at the command of Festus Paul was brought in.
verses.ALMEIDA: Então no dia seguinte, tendo vindo Agripa e Berenice, com muita pompa, e entrando no auditório com os comandantes e os homens mais importantes da cidade, trouxeram a Paulo por ordem de Festo.
verses.RVR09: Y al otro día, viniendo Agripa y Bernice con mucho aparato, y entrando en la audiencia con los tribunos y principales hombres de la ciudad, por mandato de Festo, fué traído Pablo.

verses.KJV: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men which are here present with us, ye see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews have dealt with me, both at Jerusalem, and also here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.
verses.WEB: Festus said, “King Agrippa, and all men who are here present with us, you see this man about whom all the multitude of the Jews petitioned me, both at Jerusalem and here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.
verses.ASV: And Festus saith, King Agrippa, and all men who are here present with us, ye behold this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews made suit to me, both at Jerusalem and here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.
verses.ALMEIDA: E Festo disse: Rei Agripa, e todos os homens que estais presentes [aqui] conosco, vós vedes este [homem] , a quem toda a multidão dos judeus, tanto em Jerusalém como aqui, tem apelado a mim, clamando que ele não deve mais viver.
verses.RVR09: Entonces Festo dijo: Rey Agripa, y todos los varones que estáis aquí juntos con nosotros: veis á éste, por el cual toda la multitud de los Judíos me ha demandado en Jerusalem y aquí, dando voces que no conviene que viva más;

verses.KJV: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himself hath appealed to Augustus, I have determined to send him.
verses.WEB: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and as he himself appealed to the emperor, I determined to send him,
verses.ASV: But I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death: and as he himself appealed to the emperor I determined to send him.
verses.ALMEIDA: Mas tendo eu achado nada que ele tenha feito que fosse digno de morte, e também tendo ele mesmo apelado ao imperador, eu decidi enviá-lo.
verses.RVR09: Mas yo, hallando que ninguna cosa digna de muerte ha hecho, y él mismo apelando á Augusto, he determinado enviarle:

verses.KJV: Of whom I have no certain thing to write unto my lord. Wherefore I have brought him forth before you, and specially before thee, O king Agrippa, that, after examination had, I might have somewhat to write.
verses.WEB: of whom I have no certain thing to write to my lord. Therefore I have brought him out before you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, that, after examination I may have something to write.
verses.ASV: Of whom I have no certain thing to write unto my lord. Wherefore I have brought him forth before you, and specially before thee, king Agrippa, that, after examination had, I may have somewhat to write.
verses.ALMEIDA: Do qual eu não tenho coisa alguma certa para escrever ao [meu] senhor; por isso que eu o trouxe diante de vós; e principalmente diante de ti, rei Agripa, para que, sendo feita a investigação, eu tenha algo para escrever.
verses.RVR09: Del cual no tengo cosa cierta que escriba al señor; por lo que le he sacado á vosotros, y mayormente á tí, oh rey Agripa, para que hecha información, tenga yo qué escribir.

verses.KJV: For it seemeth to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not withal to signify the crimes laid against him.
verses.WEB: For it seems to me unreasonable, in sending a prisoner, not to also specify the charges against him.”
verses.ASV: For it seemeth to me unreasonable, in sending a prisoner, not withal to signify the charges against him.
verses.ALMEIDA: Porque não me parece razoável enviar a um prisioneiro, sem também informar as acusações contra ele.
verses.RVR09: Porque fuera de razón me parece enviar un preso, y no informar de las causas.

verses.KJV: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself:
verses.WEB: Agrippa said to Paul, “You may speak for yourself.” Then Paul stretched out his hand, and made his defense.
verses.ASV: And Agrippa said unto Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth his hand, and made his defence:
verses.ALMEIDA: E Agripa disse a Paulo: É permitido a ti falar por ti mesmo.Então Paulo, estendendo a mão, respondeu em sua defesa:
verses.RVR09: ENTONCES Agripa dijo á Pablo: Se te permite hablar por ti mismo. Pablo entonces, extendiendo la mano, comenzó á responder por sí, diciendo:

verses.KJV: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before thee touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Jews:
verses.WEB: “I think myself happy, King Agrippa, that I am to make my defense before you today concerning all the things that I am accused by the Jews,
verses.ASV: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, that I am to make my defence before thee this day touching all the things whereof I am accused by the Jews:
verses.ALMEIDA: Eu me considero feliz, rei Agripa, de que diante de ti eu esteja hoje fazendo minha defesa de todas as coisas de que sou acusado pelos judeus;
verses.RVR09: Acerca de todas las cosas de que soy acusado por los Judíos, oh rey Agripa, me tengo por dichoso de que haya hoy de defenderme delante de ti;

verses.KJV: Especially because I know thee to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.
verses.WEB: especially because you are expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews. Therefore I beg you to hear me patiently.
verses.ASV: especially because thou art expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.
verses.ALMEIDA: Principalmente [por] eu saber que tu sabes de todos os costumes e questões que há entre os judeus; por isso eu te rogo que tu me ouças com paciência.
verses.RVR09: Mayormente sabiendo tú todas las costumbres y cuestiones que hay entre los Judíos: por lo cual te ruego que me oigas con paciencia.

verses.KJV: My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among mine own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Jews;
verses.WEB: “Indeed, all the Jews know my way of life from my youth up, which was from the beginning among my own nation and at Jerusalem;
verses.ASV: My manner of life then from my youth up, which was from the beginning among mine own nation and at Jerusalem, know all the Jews;
verses.ALMEIDA: Ora, a minha vida é conhecida por todos os judeus, desde a [minha] juventude, que desde o princípio tem sido entre [os de] minha nação em Jerusalém;
verses.RVR09: Mi vida pues desde la mocedad, la cual desde el principio fué en mi nación, en Jerusalem, todos los Judíos la saben:

verses.KJV: Which knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
verses.WEB: having known me from the first, if they are willing to testify, that after the strictest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
verses.ASV: having knowledge of me from the first, if they be willing to testify, that after the straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
verses.ALMEIDA: Eles me conhecem desde o começo, se quiserem testemunhar, de que conforme a mais rigorosa divisão de nossa religião, eu vivi [como] fariseu.
verses.RVR09: Los cuales tienen ya conocido que yo desde el principio, si quieren testificarlo, conforme á la más rigurosa secta de nuestra religión he vivido Fariseo.

verses.KJV: And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God, unto our fathers:
verses.WEB: Now I stand here to be judged for the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers,
verses.ASV: And now I stand [here] to be judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers;
verses.ALMEIDA: E agora, pela esperança da promessa que por Deus foi dada aos nossos pais, eu estou [aqui] sendo julgado.
verses.RVR09: Y ahora, por la esperanza de la promesa que hizo Dios á nuestros padres, soy llamado en juicio;

verses.KJV: Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come. For which hope's sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Jews.
verses.WEB: which our twelve tribes, earnestly serving night and day, hope to attain. Concerning this hope I am accused by the Jews, King Agrippa!
verses.ASV: unto which [promise] our twelve tribes, earnestly serving [God] night and day, hope to attain. And concerning this hope I am accused by the Jews, O king!
verses.ALMEIDA: À qual nossas doze tribos, servindo continuamente [a Deus] de dia e de noite, esperam chegar; pela qual esperança, rei Agripa, eu sou acusado pelos judeus.
verses.RVR09: A la cual promesa nuestras doce tribus, sirviendo constantemente de día y de noche, esperan que han de llegar. Por la cual esperanza, oh rey Agripa, soy acusado de los Judíos.

verses.KJV: Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?
verses.WEB: Why is it judged incredible with you if God does raise the dead?
verses.ASV: Why is it judged incredible with you, if God doth raise the dead?
verses.ALMEIDA: Por que se julga como incrível entre vós que Deus ressuscite aos mortos?
verses.RVR09: ¡Qué! ¿Júzgase cosa increíble entre vosotros que Dios resucite los muertos?

verses.KJV: I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
verses.WEB: “I myself most certainly thought that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
verses.ASV: I verily thought with myself that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
verses.ALMEIDA: Eu realmente tinha pensado comigo mesmo, que contra o nome de Jesus eu tinha que fazer muitas oposições.
verses.RVR09: Yo ciertamente había pensado deber hacer muchas cosas contra el nombre de Jesús de Nazaret:

verses.KJV: Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.
verses.WEB: I also did this in Jerusalem. I both shut up many of the saints in prisons, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death I gave my vote against them.
verses.ASV: And this I also did in Jerusalem: and I both shut up many of the saints in prisons, having received authority from the chief priests, and when they were put to death I gave my vote against them.
verses.ALMEIDA: O que eu também fiz em Jerusalém; e tendo recebido autoridade dos chefes dos sacerdotes, eu pus em prisões a muitos dos santos; e quando eles eram mortos, eu [também] dava meu voto contra [eles] .
verses.RVR09: Lo cual también hice en Jerusalem, y yo encerré en cárceles á muchos de los santos, recibida potestad de los príncipes de los sacerdotes; y cuando eran matados, yo dí mi voto.

verses.KJV: And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.
verses.WEB: Punishing them often in all the synagogues, I tried to make them blaspheme. Being exceedingly enraged against them, I persecuted them even to foreign cities.
verses.ASV: And punishing them oftentimes in all the synagogues, I strove to make them blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto foreign cities.
verses.ALMEIDA: E tendo lhes dado punição muitas vezes por todas as sinagogas, eu os forcei a blasfemarem. E estando extremamente enfurecido contra eles, até nas cidades estrangeiras eu os persegui;
verses.RVR09: Y muchas veces, castigándolos por todas las sinagogas, los forcé á blasfemar; y enfurecido sobremanera contra ellos, los perseguí hasta en las ciudades extrañas.

verses.KJV: Whereupon as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,
verses.WEB: “Whereupon as I traveled to Damascus with the authority and commission from the chief priests,
verses.ASV: Whereupon as I journeyed to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests,
verses.ALMEIDA: Nas quais, indo eu até Damasco, com autoridade e comissão dos chefes dos sacerdotes;
verses.RVR09: En lo cual ocupado, yendo á Damasco con potestad y comisión de los príncipes de los sacerdotes,

verses.KJV: At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.
verses.WEB: at noon, O king, I saw on the way a light from the sky, brighter than the sun, shining around me and those who traveled with me.
verses.ASV: at midday, O king, I saw on the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them that journeyed with me.
verses.ALMEIDA: Ao meio dia, vi no caminho, rei, uma luz do céu, que brilhava muito mais que o sol, e que encheu de claridade ao redor de mim e dos que iam comigo.
verses.RVR09: En mitad del día, oh rey, vi en el camino una luz del cielo, que sobrepujaba el resplandor del sol, la cual me rodeó y á los que iban conmigo.

verses.KJV: And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.
verses.WEB: When we had all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew language, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’
verses.ASV: And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice saying unto me in the Hebrew language, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? it is hard for thee to kick against the goad.
verses.ALMEIDA: E todos nós, tendo caído ao chão, eu ouvi uma voz que falava a mim, e dizia em língua hebraica: Saulo, Saulo, por que me persegues? Duro é para ti dar coices contra os aguilhões.
verses.RVR09: Y habiendo caído todos nosotros en tierra, oí una voz que me hablaba, y decía en lengua hebraica: Saulo, Saulo, ¿por qué me persigues? Dura cosa te es dar coces contra los aguijones.

verses.KJV: And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.
verses.WEB: “I said, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ “He said, ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
verses.ASV: And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.
verses.ALMEIDA: E eu disse: Quem és, Senhor? E ele disse: Eu sou Jesus, a quem tu persegues.
verses.RVR09: Yo entonces dije: ¿Quién eres, Señor? Y el Señor dijo: Yo soy Jesús, á quien tú persigues.

verses.KJV: But rise, and stand upon thy feet: for I have appeared unto thee for this purpose, to make thee a minister and a witness both of these things which thou hast seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto thee;
verses.WEB: But arise, and stand on your feet, for I have appeared to you for this purpose: to appoint you a servant and a witness both of the things which you have seen and of the things which I will reveal to you;
verses.ASV: But arise, and stand upon thy feet: for to this end have I appeared unto thee, to appoint thee a minister and a witness both of the things wherein thou hast seen me, and of the things wherein I will appear unto thee;
verses.ALMEIDA: Mas levanta-te, e fica de pé, porque para isto eu apareci a ti, para te predeterminar como trabalhador e testemunha, tanto das coisas que [já] tens visto, como das coisas que eu [ainda] aparecerei a ti;
verses.RVR09: Mas levántate, y ponte sobre tus pies; porque para esto te he aparecido, para ponerte por ministro y testigo de las cosas que has visto, y de aquellas en que apareceré á ti:

verses.KJV: Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee,
verses.WEB: delivering you from the people and from the Gentiles, to whom I send you,
verses.ASV: delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom I send thee,
verses.ALMEIDA: Livrando-te d [este] povo, e [dos] gentios, aos quais agora eu te envio.
verses.RVR09: Librándote del pueblo y de los Gentiles, á los cuales ahora te envío,

verses.KJV: To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.
verses.WEB: to open their eyes, that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive remission of sins and an inheritance among those who are sanctified by faith in me.’
verses.ASV: to open their eyes, that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive remission of sins and an inheritance among them that are sanctified by faith in me.
verses.ALMEIDA: Para abrir os olhos deles, e das trevas converterem à luz, e do poder de Satanás [converterem] a Deus; para que recebam perdão dos pecados, e herança entre os santificados pela fé em mim.
verses.RVR09: Para que abras sus ojos, para que se conviertan de las tinieblas á la luz, y de la potestad de Satanás á Dios; para que reciban, por la fe que es en mí, remisión de pecados y suerte entre los santificados.

verses.KJV: Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:
verses.WEB: “Therefore, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision,
verses.ASV: Wherefore, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:
verses.ALMEIDA: Portanto, rei Agripa, eu não fui desobediente à visão celestial.
verses.RVR09: Por lo cual, oh rey Agripa, no fuí rebelde á la visión celestial:

verses.KJV: But shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judaea, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.
verses.WEB: but declared first to them of Damascus, at Jerusalem, and throughout all the country of Judea, and also to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, doing works worthy of repentance.
verses.ASV: but declared both to them of Damascus first, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the country of Judæa, and also to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, doing works worthy of repentance.
verses.ALMEIDA: Mas sim, primeiramente aos [que estavam] em Damasco e Jerusalém, e por toda a terra da Judeia, e aos gentios anunciei que se arrependessem, e se convertessem a Deus, fazendo obras dignas de arrependimento.
verses.RVR09: Antes anuncié primeramente á los que están en Damasco, y Jerusalem, y por toda la tierra de Judea, y á los Gentiles, que se arrepintiesen y se convirtiesen á Dios, haciendo obras dignas de arrepentimiento.

verses.KJV: For these causes the Jews caught me in the temple, and went about to kill me.
verses.WEB: For this reason the Jews seized me in the temple and tried to kill me.
verses.ASV: For this cause the Jews seized me in the temple, and assayed to kill me.
verses.ALMEIDA: Por causa disto os judeus me pegaram no Templo, e procuravam [me] matar.
verses.RVR09: Por causa de esto los Judíos, tomándome en el templo, tentaron matarme.

verses.KJV: Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come:
verses.WEB: Having therefore obtained the help that is from God, I stand to this day testifying both to small and great, saying nothing but what the prophets and Moses said would happen,
verses.ASV: Having therefore obtained the help that is from God, I stand unto this day testifying both to small and great, saying nothing but what the prophets and Moses did say should come;
verses.ALMEIDA: Porém tendo eu obtido socorro de Deus, permaneço até o dia de hoje, dando testemunho tanto a pequenos como a grandes; não dizendo nada além dos que as [coisas] que os profetas e Moisés tinham dito que estavam para acontecer;
verses.RVR09: Mas ayudado del auxilio de Dios, persevero hasta el día de hoy, dando testimonio á pequeños y á grandes, no diciendo nada fuera de las cosas que los profetas y Moisés dijeron que habían de venir:

verses.KJV: That Christ should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead, and should shew light unto the people, and to the Gentiles.
verses.WEB: how the Christ must suffer, and how, by the resurrection of the dead, he would be first to proclaim light both to these people and to the Gentiles.”
verses.ASV: how that the Christ must suffer, [and] how that he first by the resurrection of the dead should proclaim light both to the people and to the Gentiles.
verses.ALMEIDA: [Isto é] , que o Cristo sofreria, e sendo o primeiro da ressurreição dos mortos, ia anunciar a luz a este povo e aos gentios.
verses.RVR09: Que Cristo había de padecer, y ser el primero de la resurrección de los muertos, para anunciar luz al pueblo y á los Gentiles.

verses.KJV: And as he thus spake for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad.
verses.WEB: As he thus made his defense, Festus said with a loud voice, “Paul, you are crazy! Your great learning is driving you insane!”
verses.ASV: And as he thus made his defence, Festus saith with a loud voice, Paul, thou art mad; thy much learning is turning thee mad.
verses.ALMEIDA: E tendo [Paulo] dito isto em [sua] defesa, Festo disse em alta voz: Tu estás louco, Paulo; as muitas escrituras te fizeram enlouquecer!
verses.RVR09: Y diciendo él estas cosas en su defensa, Festo á gran voz dijo: Estás loco, Pablo: las muchas letras te vuelven loco.

verses.KJV: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words of truth and soberness.
verses.WEB: But he said, “I am not crazy, most excellent Festus, but boldly declare words of truth and reasonableness.
verses.ASV: But Paul saith, I am not mad, most excellent Festus; but speak forth words of truth and soberness.
verses.ALMEIDA: Mas ele [respondeu] : Eu não estou louco, excelentíssimo Festo; mas eu declaro palavras de verdade e de um são juízo;
verses.RVR09: Mas él dijo: No estoy loco, excelentísimo Festo, sino que hablo palabras de verdad y de templanza.

verses.KJV: For the king knoweth of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him; for this thing was not done in a corner.
verses.WEB: For the king knows of these things, to whom also I speak freely. For I am persuaded that none of these things is hidden from him, for this has not been done in a corner.
verses.ASV: For the king knoweth of these things, unto whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things is hidden from him; for this hath not been done in a corner.
verses.ALMEIDA: Porque o rei, a quem eu estou falando livremente, ele sabe [muito bem] destas coisas; porque eu não creio que nenhuma disto lhe seja oculto; por que isto não foi feito num canto.
verses.RVR09: Pues el rey sabe estas cosas, delante del cual también hablo confiadamente. Pues no pienso que ignora nada de esto; pues no ha sido esto hecho en algún rincón.

verses.KJV: King Agrippa, believest thou the prophets? I know that thou believest.
verses.WEB: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe.”
verses.ASV: King Agrippa, believest thou the prophets? I know that thou believest.
verses.ALMEIDA: Rei Agripa, tu crês nos profetas? Eu sei que tu crês.
verses.RVR09: ¿Crees, rey Agripa, á los profetas? Yo sé que crees.

verses.KJV: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.
verses.WEB: Agrippa said to Paul, “With a little persuasion are you trying to make me a Christian?”
verses.ASV: And Agrippa [said] unto Paul, With but little persuasion thou wouldest fain make me a Christian.
verses.ALMEIDA: E Agripa disse a Paulo: Por pouco tu me convences a me tornar cristão.
verses.RVR09: Entonces Agripa dijo á Pablo: Por poco me persuades á ser Cristiano.

verses.KJV: And Paul said, I would to God, that not only thou, but also all that hear me this day, were both almost, and altogether such as I am, except these bonds.
verses.WEB: Paul said, “I pray to God, that whether with little or with much, not only you, but also all that hear me today, might become such as I am, except for these bonds.”
verses.ASV: And Paul [said], I would to God, that whether with little or with much, not thou only, but also all that hear me this day, might become such as I am, except these bonds.
verses.ALMEIDA: E Paulo disse: Meu desejo a Deus é que, por pouco ou por muito, não somente tu, mas todos os que estão me ouvindo hoje, tais vos tornásseis assim como eu sou, a não ser por estas correntes.
verses.RVR09: Y Pablo dijo: ¡Pluguiese á Dios que por poco ó por mucho, no solamente tú, mas también todos los que hoy me oyen, fueseis hechos tales cual yo soy, excepto estas prisiones!

verses.KJV: And when he had thus spoken, the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them:
verses.WEB: The king rose up with the governor and Bernice, and those who sat with them.
verses.ASV: And the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them:
verses.ALMEIDA: E tendo ele dito isto, o rei se levantou, e [também] o governador, Berenice, e os que estavam sentados com eles.
verses.RVR09: Y como hubo dicho estas cosas, se levantó el rey, y el presidente, y Bernice, y los que se habían sentado con ellos;

verses.KJV: And when they were gone aside, they talked between themselves, saying, This man doeth nothing worthy of death or of bonds.
verses.WEB: When they had withdrawn, they spoke to one another, saying, “This man does nothing worthy of death or of bonds.”
verses.ASV: and when they had withdrawn, they spake one to another, saying, This man doeth nothing worthy of death or of bonds.
verses.ALMEIDA: E reunindo-se à parte, falavam uns aos outros, dizendo: Este homem nada faz [que seja] digno de morte ou de prisões.
verses.RVR09: Y como se retiraron aparte, hablaban los unos á los otros, diciendo: Ninguna cosa digna ni de muerte, ni de prisión, hace este hombre.

verses.KJV: Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Caesar.
verses.WEB: Agrippa said to Festus, “This man might have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar.”
verses.ASV: And Agrippa said unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Cæsar.
verses.ALMEIDA: E Agripa disse a Festo: Este homem podia ser solto, se ele não tivesse apelado a César.
verses.RVR09: Y Agripa dijo á Festo: Podía este hombre ser suelto, si no hubiera apelado á César.

verses.KJV: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus' band.
verses.WEB: When it was determined that we should sail for Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan band.
verses.ASV: And when it was determined that we should sail for Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan band.
verses.ALMEIDA: E quando foi determinado que tínhamos que navegar para a Itália, entregaram a Paulo e alguns outros prisioneiros, a um centurião, por nome Júlio, do esquadrão imperial.
verses.RVR09: MAS como fué determinado que habíamos de navegar para Italia, entregaron á Pablo y á algunos otros presos á un centurión, llamado Julio, de la compañía Augusta.

verses.KJV: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
verses.WEB: Embarking in a ship of Adramyttium, which was about to sail to places on the coast of Asia, we put to sea, Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica being with us.
verses.ASV: And embarking in a ship of Adramyttium, which was about to sail unto the places on the coast of Asia, we put to sea, Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
verses.ALMEIDA: E embarcando [-nos] em um navio adramitino, estando a navegar pelos lugares [costeiros] da Ásia, nós partimos, estando conosco Aristarco, o macedônio de Tessalônica.
verses.RVR09: Así que, embarcándonos en una nave Adrumentina, partimos, estando con nosotros Aristarco, Macedonio de Tesalónica, para navegar junto á los lugares de Asia.

verses.KJV: And the next day we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.
verses.WEB: The next day, we touched at Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly and gave him permission to go to his friends and refresh himself.
verses.ASV: And the next day we touched at Sidon: and Julius treated Paul kindly, and gave him leave to go unto his friends and refresh himself.
verses.ALMEIDA: E no [dia] seguinte, chegamos a Sidom; e Júlio, tratando bem a Paulo, permitiu [-lhe] que fosse aos amigos, para [receber] cuidado [deles] .
verses.RVR09: Y otro día llegamos á Sidón; y Julio, tratando á Pablo con humanidad, permitióle que fuese á los amigos, para ser de ellos asistido.

verses.KJV: And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
verses.WEB: Putting to sea from there, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
verses.ASV: And putting to sea from thence, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
verses.ALMEIDA: E tendo partido dali, nós fomos navegando abaixo do Chipre, porque os ventos estavam contrários.
verses.RVR09: Y haciéndonos á la vela desde allí, navegamos bajo de Cipro, porque los vientos eran contrarios.

verses.KJV: And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
verses.WEB: When we had sailed across the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
verses.ASV: And when we had sailed across the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, [a city] of Lycia.
verses.ALMEIDA: E tendo passado ao longo do mar da Cilícia e Panfília, viemos a Mira em Lícia.
verses.RVR09: Y habiendo pasado la mar de Cilicia y Pamphylia, arribamos á Mira, ciudad de Licia.

verses.KJV: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.
verses.WEB: There the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy, and he put us on board.
verses.ASV: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy; and he put us therein.
verses.ALMEIDA: E o centurião, tendo achado ali um navio de Alexandria, que estava navegando para a Itália, nos fez embarcar nele.
verses.RVR09: Y hallando allí el centurión una nave Alejandrina que navegaba á Italia, nos puso en ella.

verses.KJV: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone;
verses.WEB: When we had sailed slowly many days, and had come with difficulty opposite Cnidus, the wind not allowing us further, we sailed under the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.
verses.ASV: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and were come with difficulty over against Cnidus, the wind not further suffering us, we sailed under the lee of Crete, over against Salmone;
verses.ALMEIDA: E indo navegando lentamente já por muitos dias, chegando com dificuldade em frente a Cnido, o vento, não nos permitindo [continuar por ali] ,navegamos abaixo de Creta, em frente a Salmone.
verses.RVR09: Y navegando muchos días despacio, y habiendo apenas llegado delante de Gnido, no dejándonos el viento, navegamos bajo de Creta, junto á Salmón.

verses.KJV: And, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called The fair havens; nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea.
verses.WEB: With difficulty sailing along it we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasea.
verses.ASV: and with difficulty coasting along it we came unto a certain place called Fair Havens; nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea.
verses.ALMEIDA: E tendo com dificuldade percorrido sua costa, chegamos a um certo lugar, chamado Bons Portos, perto do qual estava a cidade de Laseia.
verses.RVR09: Y costeándola difícilmente, llegamos á un lugar que llaman Buenos Puertos, cerca del cual estaba la ciudad de Lasea.

verses.KJV: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them,
verses.WEB: When much time had passed and the voyage was now dangerous because the Fast had now already gone by, Paul admonished them
verses.ASV: And when much time was spent, and the voyage was now dangerous, because the Fast was now already gone by, Paul admonished them,
verses.ALMEIDA: E tendo passado muito tempo, e sendo a navegação já perigosa, porque também já tinha passado o jejum, Paulo [os] exortava,
verses.RVR09: Y pasado mucho tiempo, y siendo ya peligrosa la navegación, porque ya era pasado el ayuno, Pablo amonestaba,

verses.KJV: And said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives.
verses.WEB: and said to them, “Sirs, I perceive that the voyage will be with injury and much loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives.”
verses.ASV: and said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that the voyage will be with injury and much loss, not only of the lading and the ship, but also of our lives.
verses.ALMEIDA: Dizendo-lhes: Homens, eu vejo que a navegação vai ser com violência e muito dano, não somente de carga e do navio, mas também de nossas vidas.
verses.RVR09: Diciéndoles: Varones, veo que con trabajo y mucho daño, no sólo de la cargazón y de la nave, mas aun de nuestras personas, habrá de ser la navegación.

verses.KJV: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.
verses.WEB: But the centurion gave more heed to the master and to the owner of the ship than to those things which were spoken by Paul.
verses.ASV: But the centurion gave more heed to the master and to the owner of the ship, than to those things which were spoken by Paul.
verses.ALMEIDA: Porém o centurião cria mais no capitão e no dono do navio do que no que Paulo dizia.
verses.RVR09: Mas el centurión creía más al piloto y al patrón de la nave, que á lo que Pablo decía.

verses.KJV: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lieth toward the south west and north west.
verses.WEB: Because the haven was not suitable to winter in, the majority advised going to sea from there, if by any means they could reach Phoenix and winter there, which is a port of Crete, looking southwest and northwest.
verses.ASV: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to put to sea from thence, if by any means they could reach Phoenix, and winter [there; which is] a haven of Crete, looking north-east and south-east.
verses.ALMEIDA: E não sendo aquele porto adequado para passar o inverno, a maioria preferiu partir dali, para ver se podiam chegar a Fênix, que é um porto de Creta, voltada para o lado do vento sudoeste e noroeste, para ali passarem o inverno.
verses.RVR09: Y no habiendo puerto cómodo para invernar, muchos acordaron pasar aún de allí, por si pudiesen arribar á Fenice é invernar allí, que es un puerto de Creta que mira al Nordeste y Sudeste.

verses.KJV: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing thence, they sailed close by Crete.
verses.WEB: When the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, they weighed anchor and sailed along Crete, close to shore.
verses.ASV: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, they weighed anchor and sailed along Crete, close in shore.
verses.ALMEIDA: E ao ventar brandamente ao sul, pareceu-lhes que eles já tinham o que queriam; e levantando a vela, foram por perto da costa de Creta.
verses.RVR09: Y soplando el austro, pareciéndoles que ya tenían lo que deseaban, alzando velas, iban cerca de la costa de Creta.

verses.KJV: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon.
verses.WEB: But before long, a stormy wind beat down from shore, which is called Euroclydon.
verses.ASV: But after no long time there beat down from it a tempestuous wind, which is called Euraquilo:
verses.ALMEIDA: Mas não muito depois houve contra ela um vento violento, chamado Euroaquilão.
verses.RVR09: Mas no mucho después dió en ella un viento repentino, que se llama Euroclidón.

verses.KJV: And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive.
verses.WEB: When the ship was caught and couldn’t face the wind, we gave way to it and were driven along.
verses.ASV: and when the ship was caught, and could not face the wind, we gave way [to it], and were driven.
verses.ALMEIDA: E tendo o navio sido tomado por ele, e não podendo navegar contra o vento, nós deixamos sermos levados [por ele] .
verses.RVR09: Y siendo arrebatada la nave, y no pudiendo resistir contra el viento, la dejamos, y éramos llevados.

verses.KJV: And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat:
verses.WEB: Running under the lee of a small island called Clauda, we were able, with difficulty, to secure the boat.
verses.ASV: And running under the lee of a small island called Cauda, we were able, with difficulty, to secure the boat:
verses.ALMEIDA: E correndo abaixo de uma pequena ilha, chamada Clauda, com dificuldade conseguimos manter o barquinho de reserva;
verses.RVR09: Y habiendo corrido á sotavento de una pequeña isla que se llama Clauda, apenas pudimos ganar el esquife:

verses.KJV: Which when they had taken up, they used helps, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, strake sail, and so were driven.
verses.WEB: After they had hoisted it up, they used cables to help reinforce the ship. Fearing that they would run aground on the Syrtis sand bars, they lowered the sea anchor, and so were driven along.
verses.ASV: and when they had hoisted it up, they used helps, under-girding the ship; and, fearing lest they should be cast upon the Syrtis, they lowered the gear, and so were driven.
verses.ALMEIDA: O qual, tendo sido levado para cima, usaram de suportes [para] reforçarem o navio; e temendo irem de encontro aos bancos de areia, eles baixaram as velas e [deixaram] ir à deriva.
verses.RVR09: El cual tomado, usaban de remedios, ciñendo la nave; y teniendo temor de que diesen en la Sirte, abajadas las velas, eran así llevados.

verses.KJV: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship;
verses.WEB: As we labored exceedingly with the storm, the next day they began to throw things overboard.
verses.ASV: And as we labored exceedingly with the storm, the next day they began to throw [the freight] overboard;
verses.ALMEIDA: E sendo muito afligidos pela tempestade, no [dia] seguinte jogaram a carga para fora [do navio] .
verses.RVR09: Mas siendo atormentados de una vehemente tempestad, al siguiente día alijaron;

verses.KJV: And the third day we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship.
verses.WEB: On the third day, they threw out the ship’s tackle with their own hands.
verses.ASV: and the third day they cast out with their own hands the tackling of the ship.
verses.ALMEIDA: E no terceiro [dia] , com as nossas próprias mãos jogamos fora os instrumentos do navio.
verses.RVR09: Y al tercer día nosotros con nuestras manos arrojamos los aparejos de la nave.

verses.KJV: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.
verses.WEB: When neither sun nor stars shone on us for many days, and no small storm pressed on us, all hope that we would be saved was now taken away.
verses.ASV: And when neither sun nor stars shone upon [us] for many days, and no small tempest lay on [us], all hope that we should be saved was now taken away.
verses.ALMEIDA: E não aparecendo ainda o sol, nem estrelas havia muitos dias, e sendo afligidos por não pouca tempestade, desde então tínhamos perdido toda a esperança de sermos salvos.
